title: Web login route grants a clinician session to any credentials when the engine is unreachable or WS_DEMO_MODE=1
description: API_URL defaults to http://localhost:8000, which is unreachable on Vercel, so tryRealLogin() returns null and the route sets a 12-hour 'demo-clinician' cookie for any non-empty email/password with no TOTP. The same happens on any non-2xx (including a legitimate 401) and on a 1.5s timeout. The portal layout only checks that the cookie parses, and the proxy forwards the demo token to the engine.
what_to_do: Remove the demo bypass from the production build (gate it behind NODE_ENV!=='production' AND an explicit WS_DEMO_MODE=1, or move demo to a separate route/deployment). Fail closed on engine errors. Require API_URL to be set (throw at module load if missing in production). Validate the session cookie's JWT signature server-side or at least reject the fixed 'demo-session-token'.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-web/src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts:4 `const API_BASE = process.env.API_URL ?? "http://localhost:8000"`, :5 `DEMO_MODE_FORCED = process.env.WS_DEMO_MODE === "1"`, :22 `if (!res.ok) return null` (any non-2xx incl. 401 -> demo), :20 `AbortSignal.timeout(1500)`, :24-26 catch -> null, :35 `DEMO_MODE_FORCED ? null : await tryRealLogin(body)`, :47-54 sets token 'demo-session-token', role 'clinician', 12h. src/lib/auth.ts:18-28 getSession only JSON.parses the cookie and checks expiresAt; no signature check. (portal)/layout.tsx:15-16 only `if (!session) redirect`. proxy/[...path]/route.ts:32-42 forwards `Bearer ${session.token}`. No middleware.ts exists in woundscan-web/src; no NODE_ENV gate anywhere. PRODUCTION.md:52-56 documents API_URL only as a Vercel dashboard setting, so an unset/mistyped value silently enables the bypass.

title: WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY silently defaults to a public string and prod terraform never sets it
description: verify_jwt accepts HS256 tokens signed with the fallback literal, so anyone reading the repo can forge admin tokens against a prod task that was not given the secret. Only the dev environment wires the Secrets Manager ARN.
what_to_do: Make _signing_key() raise at startup when the variable is unset or shorter than 32 bytes. Add data/resource aws_secretsmanager_secret 'woundscan/prod/jwt-signing' and pass it in prod secret_arns. Consider rotating to asymmetric keys so the web tier can verify without the signing secret.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-engine/src/woundscan/api/auth.py:18-22 returns literal 'INSECURE_DEV_KEY_DO_NOT_USE_IN_PRODUCTION' when WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY unset; auth/sessions.py:89 encodes HS256, :98 `jwt.decode(token, signing_key, algorithms=["HS256"])`. infrastructure/terraform/environments/prod/main.tf:77-79 secret_arns contains only WS_DB_PASSWORD and no `environment` map; dev/main.tf:49-51 + :117 is the only place WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY is wired (grep of all *.tf confirms). auth/rbac.py:38-47 gives ADMIN READ_AUDIT_LOG/EXPORT_PHI/MANAGE_USERS and api/routes/admin.py:17-19 gates only on the JWT role claim, so a forged role=admin token is fully effective. Only other setters are docker-compose.yml:37/57 and tests.

title: Engine has no real credential path; WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN is the only login and its defaults are dev@local/dev/000000
description: With the flag unset every /auth/login returns 401 (prod is unusable); with it set, a fixed user/org UUID pair is issued a CLINICIAN JWT after a plaintext compare against env defaults dev@local/dev/000000. Password hashing (auth/identity.py) and TOTP (auth/mfa.py) exist but are not wired into the route, and there is no `users` table in storage/postgres.py nor any Alembic migration despite identity.User and PRODUCTION.md assuming one. docker-compose ships the flag on.
what_to_do: Add a User SQLAlchemy model (+ initial migration) matching auth/identity.py.User, then implement DB-backed lookup in routes/auth.py using verify_password + verify_totp_code against the per-user encrypted TOTP secret, keyed by organization. Hard-fail startup if WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=1 while a prod marker (e.g. WS_ENV=prod) is set. Remove the defaults for WS_DEV_PASSWORD/WS_DEV_TOTP so dev login requires explicit values.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-engine/src/woundscan/api/routes/auth.py:44 `if not _is_dev_user(...)` is the only credential path; :55-56 fixed UUIDs ...0001/...0010; :80-91 defaults dev@local/dev/000000 (WS_DEV_TOTP_SECRET optional). docker-compose.yml:38 and :58 set WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN: "1". auth/identity.py:41-54 hash_password/verify_password and auth/mfa.py:15-22 verify_totp_code exist but the route never calls verify_password. Additional gap the finding missed: identity.py:17-18 says User is 'Stored row in users table' and PRODUCTION.md:34 says 'INSERT a users row', but storage/postgres.py defines no User/users model and no migrations/ directory exists (find returns nothing), so there is no schema to look users up from.

title: Prod environment has no ALB, TLS certificate, or domain, so no public API hostname exists for prod
description: Only dev builds an ALB with an ACM cert for woundscan.albacetemeddev.com. Prod's ECS service has no load balancer, certificate, DNS record, or WAF (the waf/ and monitoring/ modules the README lists do not exist), and is reachable only from 10.0.0.0/8, so a prod apply yields an API that neither the iOS app nor Vercel can reach.
what_to_do: Add module.alb + aws_acm_certificate (+ validation) for the StrataMetric API hostname in prod, pass target_group_arn = module.alb.target_group_arn, enable_lb = true, lb_security_group_id = module.alb.security_group_id to module.ecs, add a Route53/DNS record, and output module.alb.dns_name to feed iOS WS_API_BASE_URL and Vercel API_URL. Either add the WAF module or drop it from the README.
verifier_evidence: prod/main.tf:69-80 calls module.ecs without target_group_arn/enable_lb/lb_security_group_id and declares no module.alb, aws_acm_certificate, or Route53 record; modules/ecs/main.tf:121-129 then creates task_ingress_from_vpc from 10.0.0.0/8 only. dev/main.tf:69-101 has ALB + ACM. modules/alb/main.tf inputs (name, vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, enable_https, certificate_arn) and outputs (dns_name, target_group_arn, security_group_id) match what_to_do, and modules/vpc/main.tf:113 outputs public_subnet_ids. Also: README.md:12-13 lists waf/ and monitoring/ modules that do not exist (ls shows only alb, ecs, rds, s3, vpc). Under the stated rubric a prod apply produces a service no client can reach, i.e. a non-functional prod deploy.

title: Engine datetimes carry microseconds; Swift .iso8601 decoder rejects them, so login and measurement responses always fail to decode
description: JSONDecoder.iso uses .iso8601, and the engine emits microsecond-precision timestamps for expires_at (sessions.py:65,73 -> auth.py:67) and processed_at (pipeline.py:300,394); pydantic 2.13.5 serialises them as e.g. '2026-09-07T16:36:26.856783Z' (verified via TestClient). On devices running iOS 17.x/18.x -- the app's deployment target is iOS 17.0 -- the .iso8601 strategy (ISO8601DateFormatter .withInternetDateTime on iOS 17; Date.ISO8601FormatStyle with includingFractionalSeconds=false on iOS 18) rejects fractional seconds, so APIClient.login throws APIError.decoding after a 200 and LoginView shows 'Sign-in failed'; createMeasurement/getMeasurement would fail the same way on processed_at. On iOS 26+ the Swift 6.2 Foundation parser accepts optional fractional seconds, so the bug is OS-version dependent and can be masked when testing only on current devices. captured_at is unaffected because iOS sends it without fractions and pydantic echoes it unchanged. iOS CI runs `xcodebuild build` only, and no test decodes an engine-shaped fixture.
what_to_do: In JSONDecoder.iso use a .custom date strategy: try ISO8601DateFormatter with [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds], then fall back to [.withInternetDateTime] (or on iOS 18+ Date.ISO8601FormatStyle(includingFractionalSeconds: true) with fallback). Optionally also make the engine deterministic with a @field_serializer on expires_at/processed_at that emits second precision (or `.replace(microsecond=0)`). Add an XCTest that decodes literal LoginResponse/MeasurementResponse JSON containing '.856783Z' and switch ios-ci.yml from `build` to `test`.
verifier_evidence: APIClient.swift:146-152 sets dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601 with no custom formatter (grep of woundscan-ios finds no ISO8601DateFormatter/withFractionalSeconds anywhere). Ran the engine under TestClient (pydantic 2.13.5): POST /auth/login -> {"expires_at":"2026-09-07T16:36:26.856783Z"}; POST /measurements -> processed_at "2026-09-07T16:23:27.501115Z" while captured_at is echoed as sent ("2026-09-07T16:00:00Z"). Foundation behaviour, stated precisely: (a) classic Darwin/corelibs Foundation (iOS <= 17, the app's deploymentTarget per project.yml:5) implements .iso8601 via `_iso8601Formatter = ISO8601DateFormatter(); formatOptions = .withInternetDateTime` (swift-corelibs-foundation release/5.10 JSONEncoder.swift) which returns nil on fractional seconds -> DecodingError.dataCorrupted "Expected date string to be ISO8601-formatted."; (b) swift-foundation JSONDecoder (iOS 18+) uses `Date.ISO8601FormatStyle().parse(string)` with includingFractionalSeconds=false, and its own doc comment says "Before Swift 6.2 ... if false when parsing, fractional seconds must not be present. After Swift 6.2, fractional seconds may be present regardless of the setting" (DateComponents+ISO8601FormatStyle.swift: "fractional seconds are always optional (as of Swift 6.2)"). So decoding FAILS on iOS 17.x and 18.x and SUCCEEDS on iOS 26+ (Swift 6.2-era Foundation). LoginView.swift:59-61 collapses every error to "Sign-in failed". ios-ci.yml:30-38 only runs `xcodebuild build` (no `test`), and CaptureSessionTests never decodes an engine response.

title: Engine /auth/login has no production credential path; only the WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN stub exists
description: login() calls _is_dev_user, which returns False unless WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=1, and then compares against env-provided dev credentials with hard-coded user/org UUIDs (auth.py:55-56). The docstring says the body is 'wired to the production flow via dependency injection in app.py', but no api/app.py exists and identity.verify_password/hash_password have no callers. The engine integration tests only pass because they set WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=1. With the flag unset (as the docstring instructs for production) every iOS sign-in is a 401, independent of F1.
what_to_do: Implement a DB-backed user lookup (users table via SQLAlchemy/alembic, which are already dependencies) that calls identity.verify_password (bcrypt) and mfa.verify_totp_code against the user's decrypted TOTP secret, and use the real user/org UUIDs in create_session; keep _is_dev_user behind WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN. On iOS, catch APIError.http(401, _) vs APIError.decoding separately in LoginView.signIn so credential failures and contract failures are distinguishable.
verifier_evidence: routes/auth.py:44 gates login solely on _is_dev_user; auth.py:80-81 returns False unless WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN == '1'; auth.py:55-56 hard-codes user/org UUIDs; docstring auth.py:38-42 references `app.py` which does not exist (ls src/woundscan/api shows main.py only). grep shows hash_password/verify_password are referenced only from auth/__init__.py exports and tests/unit/test_auth.py; no users table/repository exists anywhere under src/woundscan (only rbac.py/identity.py mention 'users'). tests/integration/test_api.py:14 sets WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=1. LoginView.swift:52-62 shows one generic error for every failure.

title: Capture flow never uploads artifacts or creates a measurement; the upload/measurement API surface is dead code
description: UploadingView takes an onResult closure but renders only a spinner and never calls it, so the flow stalls at 'Uploading and processing...' forever. Grep across the app finds zero callers of presignedUploads, createMeasurement, getMeasurement, UploadService.enqueue, AuthService or MeshService. ProbeEntryView and BoundaryAnnotationView discard their results ('_ in'), CaptureSessionArtifacts is never constructed, and CapturePipeline.processFrames produces depth/confidence blobs that are never handed to an uploader. The only live engine calls are /auth/login and /measurements/{id}/mesh, and the mesh screen is unreachable because no MeasurementResult is ever produced.
what_to_do: In UploadingView (or a CaptureCoordinator observable) do: presignedUploads(woundId:, artifactType: "rgb"/"depth_burst", count:) -> PUT the CapturePipeline blobs via UploadService and await completion -> build CreateMeasurementPayload from CaptureSessionArtifacts (intrinsics, poses, fiducials, boundary, probes, s3 keys, wound_id from F5) -> api.createMeasurement -> onResult(result); route thrown errors to Step.failed. Keep the probe/boundary results instead of discarding them with `_ in`.
verifier_evidence: CaptureFlowView.swift:400-409: UploadingView stores `onResult` but its body is only ProgressView + Text and never invokes it, so `step` stays .uploading forever. CaptureFlowView.swift:31-33 pass `{ _ in step = ... }` discarding the [ProbeRecord] and BoundaryRecord. grep over woundscan-ios for presignedUploads(|createMeasurement(|getMeasurement(|UploadService|AuthService|MeshService|CaptureSessionArtifacts|.enqueue( finds only their definitions (APIClient.swift:46,60,65; CaptureSession.swift:62; Services/*). CapturePipeline.swift:83-88 returns CaptureArtifacts(depthBlobs:confidenceBlobs:poses:) which is never uploaded. The only live engine calls are login (LoginView:57) and downloadMesh (MeasurementDetailView:211), the latter reachable only from ResultView which needs a MeasurementResult.

title: /uploads/presigned returns hard-coded http://localhost:9000 URLs; no presigned-PUT implementation and no ATS exception on iOS
description: The presign route fabricates keys and returns 'http://localhost:9000/{key}'; nothing under api/ imports woundscan.storage, and S3Storage has no presigned-PUT method. On a device 'localhost' resolves to the phone's own loopback, so the PUT gets connection-refused regardless of ATS; for any other plain-http host (e.g. a MinIO box) the PUT would additionally be blocked because Info.plist declares no NSAppTransportSecurity exception. CreateMeasurementRequest requires the resulting S3 keys yet the pipeline never reads them (synthetic camera anchors), so uploads are both impossible and unused today.
what_to_do: Add S3Storage.presigned_put_url(key, content_type, expires) using client.generate_presigned_url('put_object', Params={Bucket, Key, ContentType}) and inject an S3Storage (settings from S3Settings) into /uploads/presigned so it returns https S3 URLs; have UploadService set the same Content-Type it was presigned with (and x-amz-meta-sha256 if you sign it into the Params). Also plan for the pipeline to actually consume depth_burst_s3_keys, otherwise uploads are dead weight.
verifier_evidence: uploads.py:45-49 builds keys and returns `http://localhost:9000/{key}` (verified live: upload_url = http://localhost:9000/captures/.../rgb/...bin). s3.py:95-101 exposes only signed_download_url (get_object); grep for 'woundscan.storage|S3Storage' under src/woundscan/api matches only the docstring at uploads.py:39. Info.plist:4-46 and project.yml:25-42 contain no NSAppTransportSecurity. measurement.py:67-71 requires rgb_s3_key/depth_burst_s3_keys but pipeline.py:100-121 synthesises anchors and never reads them. UploadService.swift:48-55 PUTs with no Content-Type or hash header.

title: No physical, phantom, or clinical data exists; production pipeline never ingests LiDAR depth
description: Every one of the 48 traced requirements is verified only against synthetic/analytic inputs or hand-typed scalars. A repo-wide search for any measurement data file (csv/npy/ply/pt/onnx/etc.) finds nothing. The deployed measurement path replaces the LiDAR depth field with `_synthetic_camera_anchors` — 200 random in-mask points at depth 0 and confidence 0.7 — and never calls `load_depth_frame` or reads `depth_burst_s3_keys`. Phantom submissions are held in a process-local Python list. The Tier 4/5 phantom and saline programs in validation_protocol.md are prose with no implementation.
what_to_do: Wire real depth ingestion (S3 fetch -> load_depth_frame -> projection into wound-local mm frame) into pipeline.py and delete the placeholder anchors; persist phantom scans via PhantomScanRecord (storage/postgres.py:127); then execute the Tier 4 phantom protocol on physical phantoms with caliper/water-displacement references and commit the raw data and a signed test report before any accuracy or CI claim is published.
verifier_evidence: All cited lines verified. pipeline.py:100-121 defines _synthetic_camera_anchors (200 random in-mask points, depth 0, confidence 0.7); pipeline.py:167 calls it; nothing in src/woundscan/api ever calls load_depth_frame (only tests/unit/test_capture*.py do) or reads depth_burst_s3_keys (measurement.py:71 declares the field; only test fixtures populate it). routes/measurements.py:24 builds _DEFAULT_DEPS = PipelineDependencies(product_db=...) and worker.py:43 does the same, so both sync and async production paths hit the placeholder anchors. The iOS app does upload depth bursts (APIClient.swift:46 presignedUploads; CreateMeasurementPayload.swift:10 depthBurstS3Keys) that the engine then ignores. phantom.py:15 `_PHANTOM_RECORDS: list[dict] = []`, :31 appends to it; storage/postgres.py:127 PhantomScanRecord table exists but is unreferenced elsewhere. Repo-wide find for csv/npy/npz/ply/pt/pth/onnx/h5/parquet/mlmodel/safetensors/pkl/stl/bin returns only woundscan-web/public/demo-wound.obj (a demo mesh). src/woundscan/ml/models/ and ml/training/ contain only empty __init__.py. validation_protocol.md:37-59 Tier 4/5 are prose only. .benchmarks/ is empty.

title: No design-control, risk-management, IEC 62304, cybersecurity, labeling, or predicate artifacts exist
description: Beyond the 48-row matrix (whose 'requirements' are test descriptions), six markdown docs, and a non-blocking bandit/pip-audit step, the repository contains none of the documentation a 510(k) requires: no DHF, no ISO 14971 risk file, no 62304 classification/SRS/SDS, no threat model or SBOM document, no Indications for Use or IFU, no predicate or product-code determination, no QMS/SOP/change-control records. The pytest marker text 'marks tests as 510(k)-grade regulatory validation' is aspirational.
what_to_do: Engage a regulatory lead to establish the device classification, predicate, and 62304 documentation level; stand up a DHF with real user/system requirements that the matrix traces to; produce the 14971 risk file with risk controls traced to tests; make security scans blocking and add a threat model and SBOM export; draft IFU/labeling consistent with the actual (probe-required, no-LiDAR-fusion-yet) workflow; sequence the phantom bench study (F1) and CI calibration study (F5) as the performance-testing section.
verifier_evidence: Repo-wide grep (md/py/ts/tsx/swift/yml/toml/json/tf, excluding node_modules/.next/.venv) for 14971, 62304, DHF/design history, risk management/risk file, SBOM, threat model, indications for use/IFU, predicate, product code finds only 21 CFR 830 UDI references (grafts.py:90, postgres.py:163-165) and 'IFU overlap' product-data strings (admin/products/page.tsx:16, tour/AdminView.tsx:69) — no design-control, risk, 62304, cybersecurity, labeling, or predicate artifacts. engine-ci.yml:95-97 bandit/pip-audit both `|| true` verified; pdf_report.py:171-176 CDS disclaimer verified; pyproject.toml:86 '510(k)-grade regulatory validation' marker verified. docs/ contains only six markdown files; the matrix rows are test descriptions rather than user/system requirements. Note the marketing phrase is '510(k)-ready architecture' (Hero.tsx, ComplianceSection.tsx:10) and README frames 510(k) as an 'eventual' path, which does not itself claim a submission package exists — but these prerequisites are absent, so blocker stands for a submission-readiness audit.

title: '±0.3 mm instrument precision @95%' is not derivable from any code or test
description: The engine has no precision constant, no instrument characterization, and no mm-level depth CI; max/mean depth are reported with no CI at all (pdf_report.py:104-105 prints '—'). The only CIs produced are per-measurement Monte-Carlo percentiles of volume and surface area, driven by assumed sigmas (probe 0.5 mm, camera 1.0 mm/conf) and a GP whose prior variance is hard-coded to 1 mm² and whose length scale is not optimized in production. The '±0.3 mm' figure appears as a hard-coded string in three deployed React components (Hero.tsx:74, HeroScene.tsx:82, ReportSection.tsx:275) and is additionally baked into the OpenGraph preview image by woundscan-web/scripts/generate-og.py:168 (public/og.png, og-v2.png). Depth and perimeter are also claimed to carry 95% CIs (AtAGlanceSection.tsx:19, layout.tsx:19 meta description, bin/asc-metadata.json) though the code never computes them.
what_to_do: Remove the ±0.3 mm / 'instrument precision' statements from Hero.tsx, HeroScene.tsx, ReportSection.tsx AND regenerate the OG image without the '±0.3 MM @ 95% CI' line (generate-og.py:168, public/og*.png) until a bench precision study (repeatability/reproducibility on phantoms at defined distances and lighting) has been executed and its report committed; also drop or qualify the 'depth/perimeter with 95% CI' wording in AtAGlanceSection.tsx, layout.tsx and asc-metadata.json until depth/perimeter CIs are actually computed. Any future figure must state the quantity (depth? volume?), the study conditions, and the coverage method.
verifier_evidence: Hero.tsx:74 `<HeroStat value="±0.3 mm" label="instrument precision @95%" />`, HeroScene.tsx:82 `uncertainty ±0.3 mm @95%`, ReportSection.tsx:275 `shaded band: ±0.3 mm measurement uncertainty (95% CI, Monte Carlo)` all verified. Repo-wide grep for `0.3 mm|±0.3|precision` in engine finds no precision constant (only 'subpixel precision' prose in perimeter.py:16 and math_reference.md:55). uncertainty.py:235-236 are volume percentile CIs; gaussian_process.py:170 `var_diag = 1.0 - ...` (unit prior variance, reproduced: prior sd 0.98 mm far from anchors); pipeline.py:156 sigma_mm=0.5, :191 sigma_base_mm=1.0; pdf_report.py:104-105 print '—' for depth CI. Agent missed a fourth location: woundscan-web/scripts/generate-og.py:168 bakes '±0.3 MM @ 95% CI' into the social-preview image (public/og.png, og-v2.png). Related unsupported depth-CI claims also appear in AtAGlanceSection.tsx:19, app/layout.tsx:19 (meta description) and bin/asc-metadata.json (App Store text).

title: Deployed copy makes regulatory and technical claims the code contradicts (CDS exemption, SOC 2, SAM, plane fit, no probe)
description: Deployed copy asserts the product 'operates today under the 21st Century Cures Act §3060 CDS exemption' (ComplianceSection.tsx:6; README.md:24). That exemption (FD&C Act §520(o)(1)(E)) applies only if all four statutory criteria are met, and criterion (i) requires that the software is NOT intended to acquire, process, or analyze a medical image or a signal/pattern from a signal acquisition system. The product as marketed and as built in the iOS app acquires LiDAR depth frames (ARKitCapture.swift:39-46) and segments wound photographs to produce quantitative geometry and graft sizing, so it very likely fails criterion (i) under FDA's 2022 CDS guidance; the quantitative-measurement output also does not fit the 'recommendations' framing of criteria (iii)-(iv). This is not legal advice and a final determination needs regulatory counsel (e.g. a 513(g) request), but the claim is at minimum unsupported. The site also asserts SOC 2 Type II (StatusBar.tsx:20, settings/page.tsx:90) with no attestation anywhere in the repo; SAM/sam-vit-h segmentation (TechnologySection.tsx:33-35, HeroScene.tsx:75, PipelineSection.tsx:38, ArchitectureSection.tsx:5,47) and least-squares plane-fit depth (TechnologySection.tsx:40-41) that do not exist in the engine (production uses a heuristic fallback with empty weight hash); and 'no probe in the wound bed' (AtAGlanceSection.tsx:13) while the engine returns an F-grade zero measurement without probe points (pipeline.py:169-172) and the iOS capture flow has a mandatory probe-entry step recommending 5+ anchors (CaptureFlowView.swift:14,323).
what_to_do: Obtain a written regulatory determination (counsel and/or FDA 513(g)) before using any CDS-exemption language, and remove the 'operates today under… §3060' sentence from ComplianceSection.tsx and README.md in the meantime; remove or substantiate the SOC 2 Type II statements (StatusBar.tsx, settings page); remove SAM/SageMaker, plane-fit, and no-probe statements (TechnologySection, HeroScene, PipelineSection, ArchitectureSection, AtAGlanceSection) or make the code match them; add a copy-review gate that requires a code citation for every technical/regulatory claim on the marketing site, README, and App Store listing (bin/asc-metadata.json:2).
verifier_evidence: ComplianceSection.tsx:6 CDS-exemption text verified (README.md:24 repeats it). StatusBar.tsx:20 'HIPAA · SOC 2 Type II · 256-bit AES' and settings/page.tsx:90 'SOC 2 Type II · Q1 2026' verified; repo-wide grep finds no attestation, only these two static strings. TechnologySection.tsx:33-35 SAM, :41 'plane fit'; HeroScene 'SEGMENT sam-vit-h' is at line 75 (agent cited 76); additional SAM/SageMaker claims at PipelineSection.tsx:38 and ArchitectureSection.tsx:5,47. Engine grep for sam/segment-anything/plane-fit/lstsq: none (only scipy least_squares in bundle_adjustment.py for pose refinement). boundary_segmentation.py:109-115 fallback heuristic verified; pipeline.py:169-172 F-grade without probes verified; AtAGlanceSection.tsx:13 'no probe in the wound bed' verified and further contradicted by the iOS flow (CaptureFlowView.swift:4,14,28-31 mandatory probeEntry step; :323 'Minimum 5 anchors recommended'). ARKitCapture.swift:39-46 sceneDepth verified. Statutory check: Cures Act §3060 added FD&C Act §520(o)(1)(E), which excludes a software function from the device definition only if it meets all four criteria; criterion (i) is that the function is 'not intended to acquire, process, or analyze a medical image or a signal from an in vitro diagnostic device or a pattern or signal from a signal acquisition system'. The agent's reading is accurate; FDA's September 2022 CDS final guidance applies criterion 1 to image and physiological-signal processing, and 3D wound-measurement systems have historically been FDA-regulated devices. The agent's phrasing overreaches only in stating the conclusion as settled; it should be framed as 'very likely does not qualify — needs regulatory counsel'.
root_cause: Deployed copy asserts CDS exemption, SOC 2, SAM segmentation, plane-fit depth, no-probe capture and a managed-AI-service architecture that the code contradicts.

title: Web login grants a session for any (or invalid) credentials via demo fallback
description: tryRealLogin returns null on ANY non-ok response (line 22), including a 401 for wrong password/TOTP, on a 1.5s timeout, or when WS_DEMO_MODE=1. The POST handler then falls through to the demo branch and sets a 12-hour ws_session cookie with role clinician and token 'demo-session-token' (47-54). The live site accepting any credentials is a direct consequence of this code, not a misconfiguration.
what_to_do: Delete the demo fallback from the production build path. Return 401 when the engine returns 401/403, 502/503 when it is unreachable. If a demo is required, serve it from a separate host/build with WS_DEMO_MODE compiled in and no PHI routes.
verifier_evidence: login/route.ts verified: line 5 DEMO_MODE_FORCED=WS_DEMO_MODE==='1'; line 22 tryRealLogin returns null on ANY !res.ok (incl 401 for wrong password/TOTP) and on the 1.5s timeout/catch (24-26); line 35 real=DEMO_MODE_FORCED?null:tryRealLogin; lines 47-54 the fallthrough sets a 12h ws_session cookie with role 'clinician', token 'demo-session-token', userId 'demo-clinician'. So submitting any non-empty email+password when the engine 401s on bad creds still yields a valid portal session -- a real auth bypass of the web tier. Note: the granted 'demo-session-token' is not a valid engine JWT, so the demo session sees mock (sample.ts) data, not real engine PHI; real-PHI exposure requires a forged JWT (F2+F7). Root cause overlaps F3 (no real engine auth forces demo mode).

title: Session cookie is unsigned JSON; role and identity are client-controlled
description: getSession() JSON.parses the cookie value and trusts token, role, userId and expiresAt verbatim. The portal layout gate and all /admin/* role checks compare session.role from that cookie. Any visitor can set ws_session={"token":"x","expiresAt":"2099-01-01","role":"admin","userId":"a"} and pass every server-side page gate; only the engine's JWT check (when the proxy forwards the token) stands in the way, and that check is undermined by F7. httpOnly/sameSite=strict are set but secure is only set when NODE_ENV=production.
what_to_do: Store only the engine JWT (or an opaque server session id) in the cookie and derive role/userId by verifying the JWT signature server-side on every request (or via a signed/encrypted cookie e.g. iron-session/jose). Never read role from client-supplied bytes. Set secure unconditionally.
verifier_evidence: lib/auth.ts:22 getSession does JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(c.value)) and trusts token/role/userId/expiresAt verbatim (31-37 setSession just JSON-stringifies; secure only when NODE_ENV==='production'). (portal)/layout.tsx:15-16 gates solely on getSession() truthiness; admin/audit/page.tsx:7, admin/ml/page.tsx:7, admin/products/page.tsx:8 and Header.tsx compare session.role from that same client cookie. An unauthenticated visitor can set ws_session={...role:'admin'...} and pass every server-side page gate. Because the attacker also controls the token field, they can insert a forged engine JWT (F7 default key) that the proxy forwards as Bearer, turning this into real cross-tenant PHI access (F4). Confirmed auth bypass.
root_cause: ws_session cookie is URL-encoded plain JSON with no MAC; getSession() JSON.parses it and trusts role/userId.

title: No tenant scoping on wounds, measurements, mesh, PDF, FHIR, phantom; RBAC unenforced outside admin

title: JWT signing key falls back to a public constant and prod terraform does not supply one
description: _signing_key() returns 'INSECURE_DEV_KEY_DO_NOT_USE_IN_PRODUCTION' when WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY is unset. title: Login fallback grants a session for any credentials on engine error
description: tryRealLogin returns null both when the engine is unreachable and when it answers 401/4xx/5xx, and the handler then issues a 12-hour clinician session unconditionally. On the live site API_URL is unset so fetch hits localhost:8000, fails within the 1.5 s timeout, and the fallback fires for every request (verified by the probe returning mode:'demo'). Even with a correctly configured engine, a wrong password (401) or the production default of WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN unset (all logins 401) still produces a valid portal session. The client never inspects mode:'demo'.
what_to_do: Fail closed: return 401 when the engine answers non-2xx and 502/503 when it is unreachable; only permit the synthetic session when WS_DEMO_MODE=1 is set explicitly, and in that case return and render a visible demo banner. Set API_URL on the Vercel project and add a health probe on startup that logs which mode is active.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-web/src/app/api/auth/login/route.ts:22 returns null on any non-2xx, :24-26 returns null on throw/timeout, :35 skips the engine entirely when WS_DEMO_MODE=1, :47-54 unconditionally issues a 12h clinician session with token 'demo-session-token' whenever `real` is null. login/page.tsx:26-30 only checks res.ok and never reads `mode`. Engine side reproduced with TestClient: POST /auth/login with the documented dev triple returns 401 when WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN is unset (routes/auth.py:80-81), and 401 is exactly the case the web turns into a valid session. No middleware.ts exists. The 'live probe returned mode:demo' claim could not be re-run here (no server on :4311, no live access) but is the deterministic outcome of API_URL unset -> localhost:8000 -> ECONNREFUSED -> null. Severity blocker is right: the login form accepts any non-empty credentials in every deployment that lacks a reachable engine or has a wrong password. Note the engine still 401s the demo token, so what is exposed is the portal shell, sample pages and capture endpoints, not engine data.

The iOS client defines presignedUploads()/UploadService but never invokes them, so capture binaries currently have no path to S3 from either side, and every measurement is computed without them (G3).

Wire the iOS CaptureSession flow to call presignedUploads() and UploadService.enqueue(). Consider requiring x-amz-meta-sha256 / Content-SHA256 to feed hash-on-write tamper evidence.

Reproduced: POST /uploads/presigned returned upload_url 'http://localhost:9000/captures/...'; artifact_type '../../etc' was accepted and produced s3_key 'captures/<wid>/../../etc/<uuid>-0.bin' (no validation). iOS evidence is imprecise: UploadService.swift:49-51 does PUT to job.url, but grep of woundscan-ios shows `presignedUploads(` (APIClient.swift:46), `UploadService.enqueue(` and `UploadJob(` are never called anywhere — the iOS upload flow is itself unwired, so the app does not currently attempt the PUT at all.

title: GP fusion prior is mis-specified (zero mean, fixed 1 mm^2 signal variance, unbounded lengthscale)
description: The Matern kernel has no signal-variance hyperparameter and there is no mean function, so the prior is N(0, 1 mm^2) on depths that are typically 5-30 mm and the posterior variance is capped at 1 mm^2 regardless of data. Verified: 9 probes all at 20 mm (sigma 0.61 mm) on the pipeline's ring layout give a probe-only posterior whose in-wound mean is 13.0 mm (17.7 mm midway between adjacent probes, 5.6 mm near the edge) — the exact dip depends on probe spacing (15.4 mm at 15 mm spacing, 10.1 mm at 20 mm spacing). With optimize_lengthscale=True the unbounded L-BFGS-B drives the lengthscale to ~72,000 mm on a constant field; on optimizer failure the initial params are kept but res.fun is still reported as the likelihood. No unit test exercises shrinkage.
what_to_do: Add a signal-variance hyperparameter (sigma_f^2) and a mean function (constant = sigma-weighted mean of probe depths, or a plane/TPS prior mean) and optimize (log sigma_f, log lx, log ly) with bounds (lengthscale in ~[2, 100] mm) and weak priors; multiply posterior variance by sigma_f^2; use res.x only if res.success else re-evaluate nll at the kept params; note the pipeline currently runs with optimize_lengthscale=False so the mean-function fix is the one that matters on the production path. Add tests asserting <1% shrinkage on a constant 20 mm field with probe-only anchors and that std grows with distance from anchors.
verifier_evidence: gaussian_process.py:51-60 (_matern52 has no amplitude), :136-145 (nll on raw y, no mean), :147-155 (L-BFGS-B unbounded; params kept only if res.success but nll=res.fun regardless), :169-172 (var_diag = 1.0 - v.v, so std <= 1 mm by construction). Reproduced with .venv python: 9 probes at 20 mm, sigma 0.61, probe-only, L=8 fixed -> on the production ring layout (r=10 mm in a 20 mm circle) posterior mean inside the wound averages 13.0 mm (min 5.56 mm, max 20.5 mm), 17.66 mm midway between adjacent probes; on a 3x3 grid at 15 mm spacing 15.41 mm at the cell centre, at 20 mm spacing 10.09 mm; max std exactly 1.000 mm. optimize_lengthscale=True on the constant field drove lengthscale to 72,563 mm (ring layout: 171,995 mm), matching the claim. tests/unit/test_fusion.py:59-95 only asserts |mean-5|<0.5 at one interior grid point with camera anchors agreeing, so nothing catches the shrinkage.

title: No real camera depth reaches the math: pipeline feeds placeholder zero-depth camera anchors and the capture->wound-local projection is absent
description: _synthetic_camera_anchors returns 200 anchors with depth 0 and confidence 0.7 that are passed to the GP as genuine observations on the only production path (routes/measurements.py and worker.py both call run_measurement_pipeline). Verified with 9 probes at 20 mm: fused posterior mean collapses to 3.14 mm (84% underestimate), V = 4.04 cm^3 vs 25.1 cm^3 true, and the response still receives quality grade A because the quality inputs are hardcoded. depth_burst_s3_keys, poses, intrinsics and fiducials in the request are never read; load_depth_frame, temporal_average_depth, depth_to_point_cloud, compute_scale_check and quality.compute_confidence_map have no production callers; camera-probe consistency is bypassed with cp_max_z=0.0. The iOS payload carries only S3 keys, so no client-side projection substitutes for the missing stage.
what_to_do: Implement the capture stage described in docs/architecture.md:49: fetch depth burst + RGB from S3, load_depth_frame per frame, temporal_average_depth, depth_to_point_cloud with ARKit pose, transform into the fiducial-anchored wound-local frame (new function using FiducialDetection rvec/tvec), fit the periwound skin plane to convert z to bed depth (mm), sample onto the boundary grid to produce camera_x/y/d with confidence from quality.compute_confidence_map, run check_camera_probe_agreement and feed real values into compute_quality_grade. As an immediate stopgap pass EMPTY camera arrays to fuse_gaussian_process instead of zeros — this removes the 84% collapse but the probe-only GP still shrinks toward 0 (13 mm mean on the same 20 mm case) until G1's mean function lands, so the two must ship together.
verifier_evidence: pipeline.py:100-121 (_synthetic_camera_anchors: flat_d = zeros, conf 0.7), :133-138 docstring, :167 call, :180-194 passes them to fuse_gaussian_process, :195 clips mean at 0, :258 cp_max_z=0.0, :265-274 hardcoded mean_confidence=0.7/frame_consistency=0.8/ml_conf=0.7/focus=1.0. measurement.py:69-75 defines intrinsics/depth_burst_s3_keys/poses/fiducial_separation_mm; grep over src shows depth_burst_s3_keys, load_depth_frame, temporal_average_depth, depth_to_point_cloud, compute_scale_check, compute_confidence_map, check_camera_probe_agreement have no callers outside tests (detect_aruco only via ml/fiducial_robust.py which the pipeline never imports). routes/measurements.py:16,38 and worker.py:39-44 both call run_measurement_pipeline, so this is the only production path; iOS CreateMeasurementPayload.swift:6-23 sends only S3 keys, no camera anchors. Reproduced via tests/integration/test_pipeline._make_request with 9 probes at exactly 20 mm in a 20 mm-radius circle: fused mean inside mask 3.14 mm (max 8.11, min -0.89 before clipping), V=4.04 cm^3 vs 25.13 cm^3 true (84% low), mean_depth_cm=0.32, quality grade A. At 10 mm probes: 1.51 mm mean, V=1.99 vs 12.57 cm^3.
root_cause: pipeline.py:100-121,167 synthesises zero-depth camera anchors and never downloads the S3 keys it receives; no LiDAR depth, phantom or clinical data reaches the math.

title: No trained weights, no loading path, and no ML model is ever invoked by the API
evidence: grep 'from woundscan.ml' src/ -> only inside ml/
description: No ML model is ever invoked: no weight files, no loader/config, no segmentation/tissue/probe endpoint, and api/pipeline.py never imports woundscan.ml, so every provenance record permanently says boundary/tissue='fallback-heuristic-v0', probe='fallback-none-v0' with empty sha256 (verified via a real POST /measurements). The iOS BoundaryAnnotationView shows 'ML proposes the wound boundary' but has no editor (grey Rectangle) and its only button emits a hardcoded 24-vertex 20 mm circle; moreover CaptureFlowView.swift:31-33 discards the probe and boundary records and UploadingView never calls createMeasurement, so the capture flow has no real boundary source of any kind (neither ML nor manual).
what_to_do: Decide product scope first: (a) ship without ML — remove 'ML proposal' text from iOS/web/docs, implement a real manual boundary-tracing UI in BoundaryAnnotationView, wire ProbeEntryView/BoundaryAnnotationView results into CreateMeasurementPayload and call createMeasurement from UploadingView, and set ml_segmentation_confidence=0 / drop the component; or (b) obtain/train weights, add a weights-dir/S3 setting (pydantic-settings) and startup loader, add POST /segmentation (photo -> polygon_mm + confidence using fiducial scale for px->mm) called by iOS before boundary editing, register a ModelCard per loaded model in GLOBAL_REGISTRY, and populate PipelineDependencies.*_version/_sha256 from the registry.
estimate: (a) 1-2 days; (b) 4-8 weeks incl. data/labelling, plus regulatory validation
verifier_evidence: find over repo (excluding .venv/node_modules) for *.pt/*.pth/*.onnx/*.mlmodel/*.safetensors/*.tflite -> none; woundscan-engine/src/woundscan/api/pipeline.py:22-55 import block has no woundscan.ml import, :64-69 PipelineDependencies defaults 'fallback-heuristic-v0'/'fallback-none-v0'/''; api/routes/measurements.py:24 and api/worker.py:43 construct PipelineDependencies(product_db=...) with defaults only; grep 'woundscan.ml' -> only ml/__init__.py and tests; ml/models/__init__.py and ml/training/__init__.py are one-line docstrings; no settings class references weights (only DatabaseSettings postgres.py:41, S3Settings s3.py:21; s3.py has no model loader); docs/deployment.md:58-62 env list has no weights var; woundscan-ios/.../CaptureFlowView.swift:377 'ML proposes the wound boundary', :381-383 grey Rectangle placeholder (no vertex editor), :385-391 hardcoded 24-vertex r=20mm circle; APIClient.swift:40-70 only /auth/login, /uploads/presigned, /measurements; README.md:87 'loaded at runtime from S3'; docs/ml_models.md:3 'all trained from scratch'. Reproduced: POST /measurements via TestClient -> 201 with provenance boundary_model_version='fallback-heuristic-v0', boundary_model_sha256=''. Additional: CaptureFlowView.swift:31-33 discard both probe and boundary records ('{ _ in step = ... }') and UploadingView (:400-409) never calls createMeasurement, so the iOS capture flow never submits a measurement at all.
root_cause: No weight files exist and no ML model is invoked by the API; tissue/probe models are heuristic or hard stubs.

title: All outputs served from process-local dicts; nothing persisted to S3/Postgres despite response claiming a PDF S3 key
description: All measurement, note, graft and wound state lives in module-level dicts (measurements.py:26-27, notes.py:36, grafts.py:26, wounds.py:16); a restart or second replica loses every signed note and measurement. MeasurementResponse.pdf_s3_key is a string template that nothing writes. S3Storage and the measurements/graft_applications/progression_notes ORM models exist but no route uses them, and there are no Alembic migrations at all despite postgres.py:15 saying they exist. RUNBOOK.md:471-474 and README claims of persisted PDFs with provenance are not met.
what_to_do: Create an Alembic baseline for the existing ORM models (none exists). At POST /measurements persist the Measurement row (incl. provenance_json) and put PDF/OBJ/FHIR JSON to S3 under measurements/{id}/ via S3Storage.put_object; serve exports via signed_download_url or regenerate from DB rows. Wire notes to the existing ProgressionNote model (add signed_by + hash-at-sign columns; amends_note_id already modelled) and grafts to GraftApplication. Replace dict lookups in measurements.py/notes.py/wounds.py/grafts.py with repository queries scoped by organization_id. Presigned uploads (uploads.py:44-53) must also point at real S3 or PDF/S3 work has nothing to fetch.

Repo-wide grep: S3Storage/get_session referenced only in storage/, uploads.py:39 docstring and tests (test_s3_storage.py, test_postgres_storage.py) - no route persists anything. uploads.py:44-53 returns placeholder localhost:9000 URLs. No alembic.ini/migrations/versions directory exists anywhere despite postgres.py:15. RUNBOOK.md:471-474 claims the PDF last page shows the chain. title: Tier-3 benchmarks and REQ-ACC-005 compare the integrator to itself
description: add_perlin_noise and _elliptical_paraboloid define true_volume/true_surface_area by running compute_volume/compute_surface_area on exactly the array, dx, dy and mask the tests later re-feed to the same functions; measured relative error is identically 0.0 (not ~0) for all 3 REQ-ACC-005 cases and all 10 Tier-3 cases, so 13 of 33 regulatory+benchmark cases cannot fail and the 0.5% tolerance is unfalsifiable; the 'high-resolution grid' wording in irregular_beds.py:12-15, validation_protocol.md:34-35 and regulatory_traceability.md:13 is false. Scope of severity: this is a BLOCKER for the regulatory/validation-evidence claim (a 510(k)-style validation report containing tests that cannot fail is a documentation-integrity defect a reviewer would reject), but NOT a production-deploy blocker: no runtime path depends on these tests and the geometry chain is genuinely validated by the 12 analytic REQ-ACC cases with real, small errors (volume 1e-6..1e-4, SA 1e-3..4e-2). Together with G14 (REQ-INV-005 also tautological) 17 of 33 regulatory+benchmark cases are non-informative.
what_to_do: Generate the perturbed field on a refined grid (e.g. 4x, fixed seed), integrate there for the reference, then take the test input as an exact stride of that fine field (works for both the Perlin and the FFT-fallback backend only if the noise is generated ON the fine grid; keep the noise cutoff below the coarse-grid Nyquist or low-pass before striding so the strided field is alias-free). Use V=pi*a*b*h/2 as an additional closed-form check for the unperturbed elliptical base. Record grid_n and analytic=False via GroundTruth (ground_truth.py:32-44). Re-tune tolerances to the observed coarse-vs-fine error, fix the 'high-resolution' wording in irregular_beds.py:12-15 and validation_protocol.md:34-35, reconcile validation_protocol.md:19 ('<1%') with the 0.5% assertion, and add a guard test asserting the reference was computed on a grid different from the test input (e.g. GroundTruth.grid_n > depth_map.shape[0]).
verifier_evidence: irregular_beds.py:12-15 docstring claims 'recomputed numerically on a high-resolution grid' (false: no refinement anywhere); irregular_beds.py:135-139,146-147 compute_volume/compute_surface_area on the same new_depth/dx/dy/mask stored as true_*; clinical_morphologies.py:53-57,65-66 same pattern in _elliptical_paraboloid; test_clinical_accuracy.py:41-45 and test_synthetic_accuracy.py:78-82 call the identical functions on the identical arrays; validation_protocol.md:19,34-35 and regulatory_traceability.md:13 advertise these as accuracy evidence; README.md:10 and pyproject marker text call the suite '510(k)-grade'. REPRODUCED (venv Py3.11.15, no `noise` pkg -> FFT fallback, same as CI which installs only [dev]): REQ-ACC-005 seeds 0/1/2 relV=0.000e+00 relSA=0.000e+00 exactly; Tier-3 DFU/VLU/PI3/PI4/dehiscence relV=relSA=0.000e+00 exactly. Contrast, genuine analytic cases: hemisphere relV 6.1e-05/relSA 4.1e-02, cone 2.7e-06/1.2e-03, paraboloid 3.5e-06/2.5e-03, oblate hemispheroid 6.1e-05/1.3e-02 -> the geometry code IS independently validated by REQ-ACC-001..004/006. Closed form V=pi*a*b*h/2 matches _elliptical_paraboloid numeric truth to 2.6e-06..3.0e-05, so the suggested closed form is correct. Also validation_protocol.md:19 says '<1%' while the test asserts 0.5%.
root_cause: irregular_beds.py:138-139 and clinical_morphologies.py:56-57 compute 'truth' with compute_volume/compute_surface_area on the same grid, so REQ-ACC-005 and all Tier-3 benchmarks compare the integrator to itself.

title: Integration suite validates placeholders (in-memory stores, stub presign, zero-depth camera anchors)
description: The integration suite (36 tests) runs against module-level dicts, a stub presign endpoint, and a pipeline that ignores the S3 keys and injects 200 zero-depth/0.7-confidence camera anchors. The description understates the impact: that placeholder is not a test-only path, it is what POST /measurements executes in production, and it biases the fused volume by roughly -74% (2.01 cm3 vs 7.67 cm3 probe-only, vs 6.28 cm3 analytic bowl) while still reporting quality grade A. test_pipeline.py:108's 0.5<V<30 band is wide enough to accept both the biased and unbiased values, so the suite is structurally unable to detect that persistence, S3 presigning, LiDAR ingestion and the anchor placeholder are unimplemented. Blocker for the production volume-accuracy claim (deployed endpoint returns wrong, A-graded volumes and no test can fail on it); not a regulatory-suite defect (the regulatory suite does not cover the pipeline). The code fix belongs to the API subsystem; the test-subsystem gap is a test written so it cannot fail.
what_to_do: Now, before storage wiring: (1) change test_pipeline_volume_in_expected_range to build a known synthetic bowl and assert |V - V_ref|/V_ref < ~15% (this fails today and correctly exposes the placeholder); mark it xfail(strict=True, reason='synthetic zero-depth camera anchors in pipeline.py:100-121') so the xfail flips to a failure the moment real anchors land; (2) add a test asserting that rgb_s3_key/depth_burst_s3_keys are either consumed or rejected; (3) rename/document the directory as contract tests in README.md:49 and validation_protocol.md. After storage wiring (other subsystem): moto S3 + testcontainers Postgres end-to-end test uploading a real synthetic depth burst and asserting volume within tolerance of synthetic truth.
estimate: 3-5 days test work after storage wiring exists
verifier_evidence: pipeline.py:100-121 _synthetic_camera_anchors returns 200 anchors with depth 0 and confidence 0.7; pipeline.py:166-167 unconditional call; pipeline.py has no reference to rgb_s3_key/depth_burst_s3_keys (only pdf_s3_key at :371,:412); measurements.py:26-27 module dicts and create_measurement calls run_measurement_pipeline (verified via inspect), so the placeholder is in the PRODUCTION request path with no injection point for real anchors; uploads.py:43-49 fabricates http://localhost:9000 URLs; module-level stores also in wounds.py:16, grafts.py:26, notes.py:36, phantom.py:15; api/ never references DatabaseSettings or WS_DB_*; no .delay/apply_async/send_task callers anywhere; test_pipeline.py:5-6 admits 'binary upload is not exercised'; test_pipeline.py:108 asserts 0.5 < V < 30; 36 integration nodes collected. REPRODUCED: the test's r=20 mm bowl with 9 probes at 10 mm depth -> pipeline V=2.011 cm3, grade A; with _synthetic_camera_anchors monkeypatched to return no anchors (probe-only GP) -> V=7.666 cm3, grade A; analytic paraboloid 6.28 cm3, cone 4.19 cm3. r=30/15 mm -> 6.15 cm3 vs 21.2 analytic. The fake zero-depth anchors pull volume down ~74% and the test band accepts both values.
root_cause: Integration tests exercise only the dev backdoor, in-memory stores, stub presign and zero-depth camera anchors, so they cannot detect the placeholder wiring.

title: Prod has no ALB/ACM/HTTPS — API is unreachable from the internet
description: prod/main.tf instantiates vpc/s3/rds/ecs only. No ALB, no ACM certificate, no listener; the ECS task SG falls back to the 10.0.0.0/8 rule and tasks sit in private subnets without public IPs. The prod API is reachable only from inside the VPC (10.50.0.0/16).
what_to_do: Copy the dev pattern into prod/main.tf: aws_acm_certificate (DNS validation) + aws_acm_certificate_validation for the prod API hostname, module 'alb' (source ../../modules/alb, public_subnet_ids = module.vpc.public_subnet_ids, enable_https = true, certificate_arn = aws_acm_certificate_validation.api.certificate_arn), and pass target_group_arn = module.alb.target_group_arn, enable_lb = true, lb_security_group_id = module.alb.security_group_id into module 'ecs'. Add an output for module.alb.dns_name and either an aws_route53_record ALIAS or a documented manual CNAME step (see G11).
verifier_evidence: infrastructure/terraform/environments/prod/main.tf:69-80 (module ecs called without target_group_arn/enable_lb/lb_security_group_id; no module 'alb', no aws_acm_certificate anywhere in prod); infrastructure/terraform/modules/ecs/main.tf:121-129 (enable_lb=false -> ingress only from 10.0.0.0/8), :179-182 (awsvpc network_configuration with no assign_public_ip, tasks in private subnets); grep -rn aws_lb infrastructure/ -> only modules/alb/main.tf:71, which prod never instantiates; dev pattern at environments/dev/main.tf:69-118 verified
root_cause: environments/prod/main.tf declares no alb module, ACM certificate or domain, so the prod API has no public HTTPS endpoint.

title: Prod ECS task has no environment variables and no JWT secret — engine would talk to localhost DB, wrong S3 bucket, insecure JWT key
description: Prod injects only WS_DB_PASSWORD. Every other setting takes its dev default: DB host localhost, S3 bucket woundscan-artifacts (wrong), JWT signing key INSECURE_DEV_KEY_DO_NOT_USE_IN_PRODUCTION (anyone can mint a valid clinician/admin JWT), and the prod task role has no S3/KMS permissions at all. Prod correctly leaves WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN unset (routes/auth.py:80 defaults closed).
what_to_do: Mirror dev/main.tf:115-166 in prod: environment = {WS_DB_HOST = module.rds.host, WS_DB_PORT = tostring(module.rds.port), WS_DB_DATABASE, WS_DB_USER, WS_S3_REGION, WS_S3_BUCKET = module.s3.bucket_name, WS_S3_RETENTION_DAYS = '2190', WS_CELERY_EAGER = '1'}; add data 'aws_secretsmanager_secret' 'jwt_signing' (name woundscan/prod/jwt-signing, seeded out-of-band) and WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY in secret_arns; add aws_iam_role_policy on module.ecs.task_role_name granting s3:* object/legal-hold/retention actions on module.s3.bucket_arn and kms Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey/DescribeKey on aws_kms_key.data.arn. Note the execution role also needs kms:Decrypt (G3).
verifier_evidence: infrastructure/terraform/environments/prod/main.tf:77-79 (secret_arns = {WS_DB_PASSWORD} only; no 'environment' map; zero aws_iam_role_policy resources in prod); woundscan-engine/src/woundscan/storage/postgres.py:48 host='localhost'; storage/s3.py:29 bucket='woundscan-artifacts' (prod bucket is woundscan-prod-artifacts per modules/s3/main.tf:14 with name=woundscan-prod); api/auth.py:17-23 INSECURE_DEV_KEY fallback used by verify_jwt (auth/sessions.py:92-100, HS256) so tokens are forgeable; modules/ecs/main.tf:94-97 task role has no policies attached (S3/KMS grants live only in dev/main.tf:131-166); dev pattern at dev/main.tf:115-128 verified
root_cause: prod/main.tf passes only WS_DB_PASSWORD to module.ecs (no environment map, no JWT secret, no task S3/KMS policy) so the engine falls back to localhost DB, wrong bucket and insecure key.

title: Prod task launch will fail: execution role cannot decrypt the KMS-encrypted DB secret
description: The prod DB secret is encrypted with the customer-managed data key, but the ECS execution role that pulls secrets at task start holds only secretsmanager:GetSecretValue plus the AWS-managed execution policy. Fargate will fail every prod task with ResourceInitializationError (kms:Decrypt AccessDenied). Dev is unaffected because its secret (dev/main.tf:45-47) uses the AWS-managed Secrets Manager key.
what_to_do: In modules/ecs/main.tf add variable 'kms_key_arns' (list(string), default []) and extend the task_execution_secrets policy with a second statement: Effect Allow, Action ['kms:Decrypt','kms:DescribeKey'], Resource = var.kms_key_arns (guard with count/for so the statement is omitted when empty). Pass kms_key_arns = [aws_kms_key.data.arn] from prod/main.tf (and dev if the jwt/db secrets are later moved to the CMK). Alternatively add an output 'task_execution_role_name' and attach an aws_iam_role_policy from prod/main.tf.
verifier_evidence: infrastructure/terraform/environments/prod/main.tf:53-57 (aws_secretsmanager_secret.db_password with kms_key_id = aws_kms_key.data.arn, a customer-managed key; :33-37 key has no 'policy' so default account-root key policy applies, meaning IAM grants are honored but none exist); infrastructure/terraform/modules/ecs/main.tf:75-78 (only AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy: ECR + logs, no KMS), :80-92 (task_execution_secrets grants secretsmanager:GetSecretValue only); grep -rn 'kms:Decrypt' infrastructure/ -> only environments/dev/main.tf:158, which is attached to module.ecs.task_role_name (task role, dev only), not the execution role; prod has no aws_iam_role_policy at all; modules/ecs/main.tf:223-226 outputs do not expose the execution role, so the fix must be inside the module

title: Secrets bootstrap is a chicken-and-egg: first apply fails and the RUNBOOK ordering conflicts with Terraform
description: Both environments hit a first-apply failure whichever documented order is followed: (a) follow RUNBOOK/README and pre-create the secret via CLI -> aws_secretsmanager_secret creation fails with ResourceExistsException; (b) skip that -> Terraform creates an empty secret and the deferred data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version read fails (no AWSCURRENT version), so aws_db_instance is never created. Recovery is possible without code changes (put-secret-value or terraform import, then re-apply) but nothing documents it. The DB password also lands in plaintext in state via aws_db_instance.password, contradicting README 'Terraform NEVER reads secrets'. RUNBOOK's 'Dev has no RDS' note is also stale.
what_to_do: Preferred: in modules/rds/main.tf drop the data source and 'password', set manage_master_user_password = true and master_user_secret_kms_key_id = var.kms_key_arn, and output aws_db_instance.this.master_user_secret[0].secret_arn; in ECS use valueFrom = '<secret_arn>:password::' (RDS-managed secrets are JSON {username,password}) and grant kms:Decrypt to the execution role (G3). Otherwise document the bootstrap: terraform apply -target=aws_secretsmanager_secret.db_password -var image=..., aws secretsmanager put-secret-value, then full apply; and 'terraform import aws_secretsmanager_secret.db_password <arn>' for secrets pre-created per the README. Fix README.md:40-47 and RUNBOOK.md:236-239,282-284,291-298 to match.
verifier_evidence: infrastructure/terraform/modules/rds/main.tf:64-66 (data.aws_secretsmanager_secret_version keyed on var.db_password_secret_arn), :79 (password = that data source); environments/dev/main.tf:45-47 and prod/main.tf:53-57 create aws_secretsmanager_secret with no aws_secretsmanager_secret_version anywhere (grep); RUNBOOK.md:236-239 pre-creates woundscan/dev/db-password via CLI before the first apply; RUNBOOK.md:282-284 put-secret-value only in Step 2, after the Step 1 apply; infrastructure/terraform/README.md:40-47 says Terraform never reads secrets and to create-secret via CLI (contradicted by rds/main.tf:64-66,79); RUNBOOK.md:291-298 'Dev has no RDS' is stale since commit 0e7988c 2026-05-02 (dev/main.tf:53-67 has module rds)
root_cause: Secrets Manager wiring is bootstrap-incomplete: db-password secrets have no version, dev jwt secret is a pre-existing data source, prod has none.

title: Capture flow never uploads or creates a measurement — dead-ends at UploadingView
description: UploadingView is a spinner whose onResult closure is never invoked; probe and boundary results are discarded by CaptureFlowView; CapturePipeline.capturedArtifacts is never read; APIClient.presignedUploads/createMeasurement/getMeasurement and UploadService.enqueue have zero call sites. ResultView and MeasurementDetailView are unreachable in a real session (only MeshDemoView renders a mesh). Note the engine side is equally unfinished: /uploads/presigned returns a localhost placeholder and run_measurement_pipeline ignores the uploaded RGB/depth entirely.
what_to_do: Add a CaptureCoordinator (ObservableObject, @MainActor) owned by CaptureFlowView that (1) selects a woundId via a new APIClient.listWounds() -> GET /wounds (engine already has it) shown in a picker before .warming; (2) keeps probes/boundary/capturedArtifacts from each step instead of discarding them; (3) calls presignedUploads(artifactType:"rgb",count:1) and ("depth_burst", N) and PUTs blobs through UploadService (await completion, not fire-and-forget); (4) builds CreateMeasurementPayload (capturedAt, intrinsics, keys, poses, fiducials: [], marker side/separation, boundary, probes) and POSTs /measurements; (5) sets step = .result(MeasurementResult) or .failed(message). Engine must wire S3Storage into uploads.py and replace _synthetic_camera_anchors with a fetch+decode of the depth blobs (see G8) before results reflect the capture.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-ios/WoundScan/UI/Screens/CaptureFlowView.swift:31,33 discard ProbeEntryView/BoundaryAnnotationView closures (`{ _ in step = ... }`); :35 UploadingView.onResult is the only path to `.result`, and UploadingView (:400-409) is a bare ProgressView that never calls it; CapturePipeline.swift:17,45 capturedArtifacts is write-only; grep over woundscan-ios: presignedUploads (APIClient.swift:46), createMeasurement (:60), getMeasurement (:65), UploadService.enqueue (UploadService.swift:21) have zero call sites; ResultView/MeasurementDetailView only reachable via step=.result. Engine uploads.py:49 returns `http://localhost:9000/{key}` placeholder. Engine wounds.py:62-64 does expose GET /wounds (iOS has no client for it). Engine pipeline.py:100-121,133-137 never fetches or decodes the uploaded blobs (synthetic camera anchors).
root_cause: CaptureFlowView dead-ends at UploadingView; presignedUploads/createMeasurement/UploadService have zero call sites and no wound is ever created or selected.

title: Portal URL derivation assumes an api. prefix that production does not use
description: In the documented production topology (engine on the AWS ALB at woundscan.albacetemeddev.com, portal on Vercel under a different domain) portalURL resolves to the FastAPI origin, so every embedded portal tab/row loads the engine's JSON 404 instead of the portal. This is independent of, and precedes, the cookie-format defect in G3; both must be fixed for any portal screen to work in prod.
what_to_do: Make the portal origin an explicit config value (WS_PORTAL_BASE_URL Info.plist key fed from the same xcconfig as G14; default https://portal.albacetemeddev.com or whatever the Vercel domain is), drop the api.-prefix heuristic, and document the two-origin topology in PRODUCTION.md. If a single-origin deployment is preferred instead, add ALB listener rules routing /api|/auth|/measurements|/uploads|/wounds to FastAPI and everything else to a portal service.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-ios/WoundScan/App/AppState.swift:24-32 portalURL strips an 'api.' prefix, otherwise returns the API origin; default apiBaseURL (:15) is https://woundscan.albacetemeddev.com so portalURL == apiBaseURL. PRODUCTION.md:44-58 deploys the portal to Vercel with API_URL=https://woundscan.albacetemeddev.com and a separate custom domain (e.g. portal.albacetemeddev.com); PRODUCTION.md:60-64 asserts automatic resolution. infrastructure/terraform/modules/alb/main.tf:84-139 has a single target group forwarding everything to the FastAPI container (no path/host routing to a Next.js service).

title: Login always fails: .iso8601 decoder rejects engine's fractional-second timestamps
description: Foundation's .iso8601 date strategy rejects fractional seconds. The engine's /auth/login expires_at is pydantic-serialized as e.g. 2026-09-07T16:32:52.703460Z, so JSONDecoder throws -> APIError.decoding -> generic 'Sign-in failed' for every native login. MeasurementResult.capturedAt/processedAt decode the same way and would fail identically once G1 is wired.
what_to_do: In APIClient.swift replace `.iso8601` with `.custom { decoder in ... }` that tries an ISO8601DateFormatter configured with [.withInternetDateTime, .withFractionalSeconds] and falls back to [.withInternetDateTime]; add an XCTest decoding "2026-09-07T16:32:52.703460Z" and "2026-09-07T10:00:00Z" into AuthSession/MeasurementResult; in LoginView.signIn show the underlying APIError (HTTP status/body vs decoding) instead of the fixed string.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-ios/WoundScan/Networking/APIClient.swift:146-152 `dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601` (Foundation's .iso8601 uses ISO8601DateFormatter with only .withInternetDateTime, no .withFractionalSeconds); :32-36 Res.expires_at is Date; LoginView.swift:57-60 maps every error to 'Sign-in failed'. Engine auth.py:29,67 returns expires_at=session.expires_at; sessions.py:65,73 = datetime.now(UTC)+15min. Verified with woundscan-engine/.venv (pydantic 2.13.5): LoginResponse(...).model_dump_json() -> "expires_at":"2026-09-07T16:32:52.703460Z" (microseconds always present except the 1-in-1e6 zero-microsecond instant, which emits ...:52Z).
root_cause: Engine serialises datetimes with microseconds; APIClient.swift uses .iso8601 which rejects fractional seconds, so login/measurement responses fail to decode.

title: Portal SSO broken: ws_session cookie value format does not match the web app
description: iOS seeds ws_session with the raw JWT (secure:false) but the portal's getSession() expects a URL-encoded JSON object {token,expiresAt,role,userId}; JSON.parse throws, getSession returns null, and the portal layout redirects to /login. Every embedded portal screen (3 tabs + 8 More rows) therefore shows the web login form. (In the documented prod topology the WKWebView does not even reach the portal origin; see G15.)
what_to_do: Preferred: add POST /api/auth/session to woundscan-web that accepts Authorization: Bearer <jwt>, validates it against the engine (GET /auth/me), calls setSession({token, expiresAt, role, userId}) and returns 204; have PortalWebView POST there (via URLSession with the WKWebsiteDataStore's cookie store) before loading the page. Quick alternative: build the same JSON in Swift (userId = base64url-decoded JWT `sub`, matching route.ts:57-67), encodeURIComponent it, set .secure:true for https hosts. Either way stop seeding the raw token.

title: /logout throws 500 and no sign-out exists in portal chrome; demo cookie traps users on /dashboard for 12h
description: app/logout/page.tsx is a Server Component that calls cookies().delete() during render; in Next 14.2.x the render-time cookies() object is sealed and delete() throws ReadonlyRequestCookiesError, so GET /logout yields a 500 and the ws_session cookie survives. The only link to /logout is in the legacy Header used by the three /admin pages; the portal chrome (Sidebar, Topbar user chip, MobileNav) has no sign-out at all, so ordinary clinicians have no way to end a session. Because app/page.tsx redirects any session holder to /dashboard, a user who has signed in cannot reach the marketing site until the cookie expires (12h for demo sessions, engine expires_at for real ones) or clears cookies. They are not locked out of the portal itself.
what_to_do: Delete app/logout/page.tsx and add app/logout/route.ts with a GET (and POST) handler: `await clearSession(); return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/', req.url))` (route handlers get mutable cookies; note clearSession must use cookies().delete or set with maxAge 0 on the same path). Alternatively expose a Server Action `signOut` and call it from a <form>. Add a 'Sign out' control to the Topbar user chip, the Sidebar footer, and the MobileNav drawer footer. When session.token is a real JWT also POST /auth/logout to the engine (engine auth.py:94-106) so the audit chain records LOGOUT. Add a vitest or Playwright check that GET /logout returns 30x and clears ws_session.

title: iOS API host is hardcoded to the old-brand domain and the WS_API_BASE_URL override is defined nowhere
description: AppState.defaultAPIBaseURL() falls back to https://woundscan.albacetemeddev.com; PRODUCTION.md:132-138 documents that as the intended prod URL with WS_API_BASE_URL as an (unused) dev override, so the shipped app (CFBundleVersion 9) has no per-configuration switch and its 'prod' host is only provisioned by the dev terraform ACM cert/ALB. portalURL strips an 'api.' prefix the host lacks, so embedded PortalTab loads the FastAPI host rather than stratametricai.com, and PortalWebView seeds a raw JWT as ws_session whereas woundscan-web/src/lib/auth.ts expects a JSON-encoded Session, so getSession() returns null and the WebView always lands on /login.
what_to_do: In project.yml add `info.properties: WS_API_BASE_URL: $(WS_API_BASE_URL)` and `WS_PORTAL_BASE_URL: $(WS_PORTAL_BASE_URL)`, set the values under `targets.WoundScan.settings.configs.Debug/Release` (or via xcconfig), re-run `xcodegen generate` and commit the regenerated tracked project.pbxproj. Point Release at the prod API hostname once F8 provisions it. Replace the api.-prefix heuristic with the explicit WS_PORTAL_BASE_URL. AppState.swift:24-32 strips 'api.' so portalURL == the API host. PortalWebView.swift:55-62 seeds raw JWT as ws_session with secure:false; web src/lib/auth.ts:22 JSON.parses the cookie, so a raw JWT throws -> null -> redirect to /login. title: Embedded-portal SSO is broken: ws_session cookie value format does not match the portal, and portalURL resolves to the API host
description: PortalWebView seeds a cookie named ws_session whose value is the raw engine JWT (secure:false, 12h expiry). Also fix prod terraform to actually attach an ALB (target_group_arn/enable_lb) since the iOS app cannot reach the prod API otherwise.

title: REQ-ACC-005 and all Tier-3 'clinical morphology' benchmarks are tautological (truth = function under test on the same grid)
description: `add_perlin_noise` sets `true_volume`/`true_surface_area` by calling `compute_volume`/`compute_surface_area` on the identical depth array, dx, dy, and mask that the test then passes to the same functions; `_elliptical_paraboloid` does the same. Verified independently: relative error is exactly 0.000e+00 for all three REQ-ACC-005 seeds and all five Tier-3 morphologies. The docstrings claim truth is 'recomputed numerically on a high-resolution grid' — it is the same grid, and synthesis/ground_truth.py (a wrapper that copies the same fields) provides no independent reference either. These 13 tests (3 parametrized REQ-ACC-005 + 10 benchmarks) cannot fail on any geometry regression and provide no evidence for the '<0.5% vs numerical truth' tolerance the matrix and protocol cite. The analytic Tier-1 cases (REQ-ACC-001..004, 006) remain genuine because analytic_shapes.py carries closed-form values.
what_to_do: Compute reference values on a genuinely finer grid (e.g. 4x resolution with an independent integrator such as trapezoid/Richardson extrapolation) and downsample the depth field for the test input; for the elliptical paraboloid use the closed form for volume (V = π·a·b·h/2) — surface area of an elliptical paraboloid has no elementary closed form, so it needs the high-resolution numerical reference; populate GroundTruth.analytic=False/grid_n honestly via synthesis/ground_truth.py; re-derive the tolerance budget from the resulting errors and update REQ-ACC-005 and validation_protocol.md Tier 3 accordingly.
verifier_evidence: Reproduced with .venv python: relative error is exactly 0.000e+00 for REQ-ACC-005 seeds 0/1/2 and for all five morphologies (DFU, VLU, PI stage 3/4, surgical dehiscence). irregular_beds.py:135-148 sets true_volume/true_surface_area via compute_volume/compute_surface_area on the same new_depth/dx/dy/mask; :12-15 and :113-114 docstrings claim 'high-resolution grid' / 'fine grid (Simpson's rule)'. clinical_morphologies.py:53-57 does the same in _elliptical_paraboloid. The agent missed src/woundscan/synthesis/ground_truth.py, but it is only a dataclass wrapper (compute_ground_truth copies wound.true_* fields, ground_truth.py:55-64) and its grid_independence_check helper is not used by any regulatory or benchmark test — so it does not refute the finding. Analytic shapes (hemisphere/cone/paraboloid/hemispheroid) do carry closed-form truth (analytic_shapes.py:184-201), so REQ-ACC-001..004/006 are genuine; only ACC-005 and Tier 3 are tautological. traceability.md:13 and validation_protocol.md:30-35 verified. Test count: 3 parametrized ACC-005 + 5 morphology + 5 DFU-population = 13, matches.

title: Traceability checker verifies only that a test file exists; 'bidirectional' coverage claim is false
description: The checker parses the matrix, rejects duplicate REQ IDs, and checks `Path(test_path.split('::')[0]).exists()`. It never resolves the class/method node, never runs pytest, and never checks that every test maps to a requirement. All 48 nodes do currently resolve (verified independently), but 298 of 346 distinct collected test nodes have no requirement, so the matrix, the protocol, README.md:30, and two deployed marketing statements describing it as 'bidirectional' are inaccurate. The traceability script itself runs only in regulatory.yml, which triggers on pull_request only; the regulatory tests do also run on pushes to main via engine-ci.yml, so the gap is limited to the coverage check, not the tests.
what_to_do: Extend check_traceability.py to run `pytest --collect-only -q -o addopts=''` and assert every matrix node ID is collected and (optionally by marker) every regulatory/benchmark node appears in the matrix; fail the build otherwise; either add `push: branches: [main]` to regulatory.yml or move the traceability step into engine-ci.yml's unit-and-regulatory job; correct the 'bidirectional' wording in docs, README.md and web copy until the reverse check exists.
verifier_evidence: check_traceability.py:1-8 docstring and :53-55 (`file_part = test_path.split('::')[0]; if not full.exists()`) verified — only file existence is checked. Independently ran `pytest --collect-only -q -o addopts=''`: 368 collected nodes, 346 distinct after stripping parametrization; all 48 matrix nodes resolve; 298 distinct nodes have no requirement (308 counting parametrized instances). traceability.md:3-5 'Bidirectional mapping… every test → at least one requirement', validation_protocol.md:61-65 'Bidirectional coverage is enforced by build-time check', ComplianceSection.tsx:10 and TechnologySection.tsx:47 'bidirectional regulatory traceability matrix' all verified; README.md:30 repeats it. regulatory.yml:3-6 is pull_request-only — verified — BUT engine-ci.yml:3-12 triggers on push to main/claude/* and its unit-and-regulatory job runs `pytest -q tests/unit tests/regulatory tests/benchmarks`, so the regulatory tests themselves do run on main pushes; only the traceability script is PR-only.

title: 95% CI calibration is never tested and its inputs are unfitted constants
description: REQ-INV-005 ('95% CI contains truth') asserts only that the unperturbed point estimate lies inside its own MC percentile interval for 4 seeds — essentially guaranteed by construction; the unit-test comment (test_geometry.py:301-305) states it is checked against 'the discretized volume estimate (not the analytic truth)'. No test measures coverage probability, contradicting the protocol's '≥95%' claim. In production the GP length scale is frozen at 8 mm (optimize_lengthscale=False), the kernel amplitude is fixed at 1 mm², probe/camera sigmas are literals (0.5 mm, 1.0 mm/conf), and n_samples is 300 (math_reference.md:161 says 1000). The CI is furthermore produced by uncertainty.py option 2 (smoothed white noise scaled by the GP's pointwise std), not by sampling the GP posterior. The CI therefore reflects assumptions, not measured error.
what_to_do: Add a coverage test: for N synthetic wounds with known analytic truth, inject sensor noise via synthesis/degradation.py (add_sensor_noise / degrade_synthetic_wound exist), run the full fuse_gaussian_process -> compute_*_with_uncertainty path, and assert empirical coverage in [93%,97%]; fit the GP amplitude and length scale (optimize_lengthscale=True or a validated fixed value from phantom data); document n_samples and all sigma constants in math_reference.md and the PDF methodology text.
verifier_evidence: test_property_invariants.py:73-83 verified: asserts only `ci_95_low <= V_point <= ci_95_high` where V_point is compute_volume on the unperturbed field, for seeds 0-3. tests/unit/test_geometry.py:301-305 comment 'near the discretized volume estimate (not the analytic truth)' verified. validation_protocol.md:28 '95% CIs contain the truth ≥95%' and traceability.md:19 verified. gaussian_process.py:93 initial_lengthscale_mm=8.0, :170 unit prior variance verified; pipeline.py:193 optimize_lengthscale=False, :225-237 n_samples=300 verified; reproduced with the venv: correlation_length_mm=8.0 and prior sd 0.98 mm. math_reference.md 'Default: 1000 samples' is at line 161 (agent cited 160, off by one). Additionally the pipeline CI does not use the GP posterior covariance at all: it passes depth_std + correlation_length to uncertainty.py option 2 (Gaussian-smoothed white noise), so the CI is a heuristic propagation, not a posterior sample.

title: PDF report discloses a methodology the production code does not follow and prints fabricated quality sub-scores
description: The Methodology paragraph says fusion runs 'over probe + camera anchors' (camera anchors are fake zeros) and uncertainty is 'sampling from posterior' (it is smoothed white noise with an unfitted correlation length). The Quality Grade table is computed from constants (mean_confidence 0.7, camera_probe_max_z 0.0, frame_consistency 0.8, ml_segmentation 0.7, focus 1.0) rather than from the capture. Tissue is assumed 'granulation' for all probes; graft indication is hard-coded 'DFU'; patient_token is 'opaque' and clinician_id is 'dev'; provenance is rendered from a Python dict repr split on commas. Depth values carry no CI although the web claims every measurement does.

title: Validation and ML docs describe programs and models that do not exist in code
description: validation_protocol.md lists moderate-hemispheroid and cylindrical-pit cases under the `-m regulatory` Tier 1 table, but those live only in unit tests without the regulatory marker; the property-invariants docstring promises rotation invariance that has no test; Tier 4 phantom and Tier 5 saline programs are unimplemented; ml_models.md claims three models 'trained from scratch on labeled wound datasets' with model cards and a performance dashboard, yet no weights, cards, or metrics exist and the admin page shows '—'. title: Provenance accepts empty model hashes and 'unknown' git SHA silently
description: hash_weights_file returns '' for a missing file (and a test enshrines that behaviour), PipelineDependencies default every model SHA to '' and git_sha to 'unknown', and the provenance builder records them without complaint. Both production construction sites — routes/measurements.py:24 (_DEFAULT_DEPS) and worker.py:43 — use those defaults, so every provenance record currently emitted pins neither code nor weights, contradicting the reproducibility claim in TechnologySection.tsx:33-34,47.
