title: Upload/measurement input surface: placeholder presigned URLs, unvalidated key segments, unbounded payload sizes, synchronous heavy compute
description: /uploads/presigned fabricates http://localhost:9000 URLs; S3Storage (which does implement hash-on-write, object lock, 300s presigned GETs) has no caller in src. artifact_type is an arbitrary string spliced into the S3 key (path traversal / prefix escape once wired) and file_count has no ceiling. CreateMeasurementRequest imposes no max length on poses, fiducials, probe_measurements, depth_burst_s3_keys or boundary vertices, and does not verify that the referenced S3 keys belong to the caller's wound; the GP fusion and two 300-sample Monte Carlo runs execute inline in the request thread. The Celery task exists but is never enqueued (no .delay/apply_async in src). iOS PUTs blobs to whatever URL the engine returns.
what_to_do: Wire S3Storage with per-org key prefixes; validate artifact_type against an enum and cap file_count; add Field(max_length=...) on all lists and a body-size limit; verify S3 key ownership; move the pipeline to the Celery worker with a job-status endpoint.

title: Prod terraform has no ALB/TLS, no JWT secret, no DB environment, no task S3/KMS policy; cannot serve traffic as written
description: Only the dev environment declares module.alb with an ACM cert, HTTPS listener, 301 redirect and TLS1.3 policy. Prod declares vpc/s3/rds/ecs only: enable_lb defaults false so the task SG opens 8000 to 10.0.0.0/8, there is no public entry point, no WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY secret, no WS_DB_HOST/WS_S3_* environment (engine defaults to localhost), and no IAM policy granting the task S3/KMS access. Whatever the probe reached in production is therefore not this terraform. Even in dev the ALB accepts 0.0.0.0/0, has no access_logs block and no WAF association.
what_to_do: Promote the dev ALB/ACM/ECS wiring to prod with ingress_cidrs tightened or WAF attached, add access_logs to an encrypted bucket, inject WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY and DB/S3 env, add the task IAM policy, and document which stack actually backs the live host.

title: In-VPC transport not enforced: no RDS force_ssl/sslmode, plaintext Redis for Celery results holding measurement PHI
description: The RDS parameter group sets pgaudit/log params but not rds.force_ssl=1, and the SQLAlchemy DSN carries no sslmode, so Postgres traffic may be cleartext inside the VPC. Celery broker and result backend default to redis:// with no TLS or password; the task returns the full MeasurementResponse (wound_id, measurements, provenance) into the result backend with Celery's default 1-day result_expires. No ElastiCache/Redis resource exists in terraform and the API never enqueues the task, so this is latent rather than live. ALB to task is HTTP.
what_to_do: Set rds.force_ssl=1 and sslmode=verify-full with the RDS CA bundle; when the worker is enabled use rediss:// with AUTH on an encrypted ElastiCache cluster, set result_expires short, and store only a job id/status in the backend with results written to Postgres.
verifier_evidence: rds/main.tf:97-116 parameter group sets shared_preload_libraries/log_statement=ddl/log_min_duration but NOT rds.force_ssl=1. postgres.py:55-59 dsn has no sslmode. worker.py:20-28 Celery broker/backend default redis:// (no TLS/password) and the task returns the full MeasurementResponse (worker.py:45) into the result backend. No ElastiCache resource in terraform and the API never enqueues, so latent not live. alb->task listener is HTTP (alb/main.tf). Accurate; major.

title: Encryption at rest mostly correct, but logs and Performance Insights lack CMK and object lock is GOVERNANCE mode
description: RDS storage, S3 default encryption and Secrets Manager all use the rotating CMK (verified). However the ECS application log group and VPC flow-log group have no kms_key_id, Performance Insights has no performance_insights_kms_key_id, and there is no bucket policy denying aws:SecureTransport=false or non-KMS PutObject. Object lock uses GOVERNANCE mode both in terraform and in S3Storage.put_object, which any principal with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention can override; the dev task role is additionally granted s3:DeleteObject and s3:PutObjectRetention. put_object relies on the bucket default rather than explicitly requesting SSE-KMS.
what_to_do: Add kms_key_id to both log groups and to Performance Insights; add a bucket policy requiring TLS and aws:kms; switch object lock to COMPLIANCE for the 6-year retention tier; drop DeleteObject/PutObjectRetention from the task role; pass ServerSideEncryption='aws:kms' explicitly in put_object.
verifier_evidence: Verified positives and gaps: rds/main.tf:76-77 storage_encrypted+kms, s3/main.tf:30-39 SSE-KMS default, secrets use the CMK. Gaps confirmed: ecs/main.tf:55-58 aws_cloudwatch_log_group.app has no kms_key_id; vpc/main.tf:24-27 flow-log group no kms_key_id; rds/main.tf:84 performance_insights_enabled=true with no performance_insights_kms_key_id; s3 module has no bucket policy denying aws:SecureTransport=false or non-KMS PutObject; object lock mode=GOVERNANCE in s3/main.tf:46 and s3.py put_object; dev task role (dev/main.tf:139-147) grants s3:DeleteObject and s3:PutObjectRetention; put_object relies on bucket default rather than explicit SSE-KMS. Accurate; major.

title: Backups and detective controls: 7-day RDS retention, no AWS Backup, no CloudTrail, pgaudit preloaded but not configured, hard S3 expiry at 6y
description: Prod RDS: automated backups 7 days, multi-AZ, deletion protection and final snapshot are set (good) but there is no aws_backup_plan/vault, no cross-region copy and no snapshot-level 6-year retention for the audit tables. pgaudit is in shared_preload_libraries but no pgaudit.log parameter is set, so DB-level audit emits nothing; log_statement=ddl only. No aws_cloudtrail resource exists in either environment (GuardDuty/SecurityHub only in prod; VPC flow logs in both). The S3 lifecycle expires current and noncurrent versions at exactly retention_days (2190) with no legal-hold carve-out.

Accurate; major.

title: Log redaction is a fixed-key stub that is never called; raw exception text and resource UUIDs reach logs and metrics
description: ErrorReporter.report only blanks nine literal keys when they appear at the top level of an explicitly passed context dict, then logs error_message=str(exc) unredacted (pydantic ValidationErrors embed submitted values such as patient_token and notes). capture_exception has no caller anywhere in src, so even that partial redaction never executes; unhandled exceptions go through FastAPI's default path. The structlog pipeline has no redaction processor and no request-id binding. Tracing is a no-op unless the OTel SDK is importable, in which case OTLPSpanExporter targets localhost:4318 with no collector in terraform. See F9 for /metrics path labels.
what_to_do: Add a structlog processor that hashes/strips known PHI fields and any value matching MRN/DOB/email patterns; register a global exception handler that calls capture_exception; bind a request id; set uvicorn access_log=False or a redacting formatter; ship OTel only to a HIPAA-eligible collector.

Accurate; major.

title: Phone-handoff capture API is unauthenticated and stores wound photos + patient labels in Next.js process memory
description: None of the four capture-session handlers call getSession(). Anyone can create unlimited sessions (each able to hold a 7MB data URL for up to 60 minutes) with a free-text patientLabel, and anyone holding a session id can read the photo and notes. The id is 64 bits of CSPRNG (adequate against brute force) but it is the only secret and is carried in the /m/[id] URL and QR code, so it lands in browser history, referrers and access logs. Images are plaintext in globalThis.__captureStore, not shared across replicas, never encrypted, never audited, and never forwarded to the engine or S3.
what_to_do: Require the portal session on create/poll/image, bind the mobile upload to a short-lived signed token embedded in the QR, cap concurrent sessions, store images in S3 (SSE-KMS, short TTL) rather than memory, and write audit entries for image reads.
verifier_evidence: None of capture/sessions/route.ts (POST createSession), sessions/[id]/route.ts (GET), [id]/upload/route.ts (POST), [id]/image/route.ts (GET) call getSession -- verified, they only touch captureStore. captureStore.ts:45-55 createSession takes a free-text patientLabel and imposes no concurrency cap; randomId (80-86) is 8 bytes = 64 bits CSPRNG; images held as data URLs in globalThis.__captureStore (32-33), plaintext, never encrypted/audited/forwarded to engine or S3. TTL 30 min (25) not 60 as the finding says (minor). Upload route DOES cap at ~7MB/5MB (upload/route.ts:16-18) -- so 'unbounded payload' is inaccurate but the finding already notes the 7MB figure. The id is carried in /m/[id] (m/[id]/page.tsx) and its QR. Core claim (unauthenticated PHI capture endpoints, in-memory plaintext images) holds; major.

title: Web proxy is an authenticated open relay to every engine path with no size cap; masks upstream auth failures
description: forward() attaches the cookie's token as a Bearer header and relays GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to `${API_BASE}/${path}` for any path, including /admin/*, /docs, /metrics, /phantom and /auth/logout; the only gate is getSession(), which F2 shows is forgeable. It is not an SSRF to arbitrary hosts (API_BASE is fixed) and path segments are normalised by fetch, but the request body is buffered without limit, the 3-second timeout will abort real pipeline calls, and any non-2xx (including 401/403) on a mesh path is replaced by the bundled demo OBJ, hiding authorization failures from the user and from monitoring.
what_to_do: Allowlist the proxied prefixes (measurements, wounds, notes, grafts, reimbursement, uploads), reject others with 404, cap body size, propagate upstream 401/403 unchanged, and remove the demo-mesh fallback from production builds.
verifier_evidence: proxy/[...path]/route.ts:31-42 forward() gates only on getSession() (forgeable per F2), sets Authorization: Bearer session.token, and relays GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE to `${API_BASE}/${path}` for ANY path (no allowlist -- /admin/*, /docs, /metrics, /phantom, /auth/logout all reachable). Body buffered without limit via req.arrayBuffer() (57); AbortSignal.timeout(3000) (54) will abort real pipeline calls; 503 empty-envelope on unreachable (71); mesh GETs replace ANY non-2xx (incl 401/403) with the bundled demo OBJ (66-67, 76-77), hiding auth failures. Not an arbitrary-host SSRF (API_BASE fixed). Accurate; major.

title: Web headers: no CSP; Permissions-Policy disables the camera on the app's own capture page; mock PHI-like data rendered on auth failure
description: Web security headers are mostly set (HSTS/nosniff/X-Frame-Options/Referrer-Policy/Permissions-Policy) but there is no Content-Security-Policy, and the blanket Permissions-Policy 'camera=()' suppresses getUserMedia on the app's own /m/[id] capture page. There is no middleware.ts, so route protection relies on each page calling getSession(); on engine failure wounds/[id]/page.tsx silently renders fabricated mock progression data (from sample.ts) instead of surfacing the 401/403, so an operator cannot distinguish an auth/backend failure from real data. Separately, sample.ts contains fabricated patient names/MRNs rendered by other portal pages. (The wound-detail page itself falls back to mock progression, not MRNs.)
what_to_do: Add a nonce-based CSP via middleware; scope Permissions-Policy so /m/* allows camera=(self); surface engine 401/403 as a visible error instead of mock data; keep sample.ts out of the production bundle.
verifier_evidence: next.config.mjs:5-18 sets HSTS/nosniff/X-Frame-Options DENY/Referrer-Policy/Permissions-Policy on /(.*) and suppresses X-Powered-By; no Content-Security-Policy -- confirmed. Permissions-Policy 'camera=()' (line 14) applies to every route including /m/[id], and MobileCapture.tsx:44/65 calls getUserMedia -- confirmed blanket camera block. No middleware.ts (find confirms none), so protection is per-page getSession; wounds/[id]/page.tsx:22-37/41 uses token=session?.token??'' and fetchJson falls back on non-ok. One correction: the wound-detail page's fallback is mockProgression (fabricated trajectory/measurement data, sample.ts:137+), NOT patient MRNs; the MRN-bearing PATIENTS array (sample.ts:22-35) is rendered by other portal pages (dashboard/lists), not this page. Also the (portal) layout redirects when there is no session, so this page only 'proceeds' for an authenticated/demo session whose token the engine rejects. Core claim (no CSP; camera policy self-defeating on /m/*; mock data silently shown on engine failure, indistinguishable from real) holds. Severity major is defensible (no CSP on a PHI app + auth-failure masking).

title: Engine has no production authentication path; login is a static env-gated dev credential
description: The engine has no production authentication backend: login() only supports the env-gated dev credential (WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN + dev@local/dev/000000, hardcoded user/org/role), there is no users table, and bcrypt/TOTP helpers are used only by tests. In production either nobody can authenticate (web then falls to F1 demo mode) or a single shared credential logs everyone in as one fixed identity/org. This is authentication-not-implemented (a missing required control); the directly exploitable auth bypass is tracked in F7 (public default signing key) and F1 (web demo fallback).

title: All PHI persistence is in-process dicts; Postgres models, migrations, RLS and column encryption are unwired or absent
description: All PHI persistence is in-process Python dicts; storage.postgres (models, get_session) is never imported by any route. The RLS / column-level encryption / Alembic migrations promised in the module docstring do not exist (no migrations directory, no CREATE POLICY, no encrypt/decrypt for the encrypted_* columns), the default DB password is 'woundscan', and with prod desired_count=2 each replica holds disjoint data and a deploy/scale event erases all wounds/measurements/notes and the audit log. title: Audit log is in-memory per process and the tamper-evident chain is never verified or persisted
description: The audit log is a single in-memory AuditLogger per process; the AuditLogEntry table is never written. append_to_chain runs per entry but only self_hash is retained, so verify_chain can never be run against stored entries; verify_chain has no non-test caller. Any restart resets the chain and any second replica keeps a colliding independent chain, neither detectable. Read access logging is also incomplete (no entry for read_wound/list_wounds/progression, graft list/get, or admin reads) and login audit metadata stores the workforce email. This is a broken/ineffective required control (audit integrity), not a PHI exposure or auth bypass.

title: Server-side sessions, logout revocation, idle timeout and MFA are implemented but never invoked
description: SessionStore (put/get/delete/touch) is instantiated only in tests; no Redis implementation exists despite the docstring. get_identity checks signature and exp only and ignores the sid claim, so /auth/logout merely writes an audit row and the token stays valid until exp. There is no refresh/touch, so exp is a fixed 15 minutes from issuance; combined with F1 the web silently drops into demo mode when a real session expires. TOTP is verified only in the dev path when WS_DEV_TOTP_SECRET is set; otherwise it is a string compare against '000000'.
what_to_do: Back SessionStore with Redis/Postgres; have get_identity look up sid and 401 if missing/expired; have logout delete it; implement sliding idle timeout via touch(); enforce per-user TOTP secrets and recovery codes.

title: Engine API hardening absent: wildcard CORS, public /docs and /metrics leaking resource IDs, no rate limiting, no security headers, no exception handler
description: CORSMiddleware allows every origin/method/header; Swagger UI is served at /docs; /metrics needs no auth and the request-duration histogram is labelled with the raw request path, so measurement and wound UUIDs (and their existence) are exposed to any scraper and label cardinality is unbounded. There is no rate limiter (login brute force, pipeline CPU exhaustion), no TrustedHost/host-header check, no request-size cap, no security-header middleware, and no global exception handler; 'Malformed token: {e}' echoes parser internals.
what_to_do: Restrict allow_origins to the portal origin; disable /docs in prod; put /metrics on a separate port or behind auth/IP allowlist and normalise the route label to the matched template (request.scope['route'].path); add slowapi or ALB/WAF rate limits on /auth/login and /measurements; add a generic 500 handler that logs via capture_exception and returns an opaque body.
verifier_evidence: main.py:42-48 CORSMiddleware allow_origins/methods/headers=['*'] (allow_credentials=False, which somewhat limits browser risk since the engine uses Bearer not cookies); docs_url='/docs' (38); /metrics (63-67) has no auth; metrics_middleware (50-60) labels the histogram with route=request.url.path (raw path), so measurement/wound UUIDs and their existence leak to any scraper and label cardinality is unbounded. No rate limiter, no TrustedHost, no request-size cap, no security-header middleware, and no global exception handler; get_identity returns detail=f'Malformed token: {e}' (auth.py:46). All accurate; major.
root_cause: create_app() applies no hardening: wildcard CORS, unauthenticated /docs and /metrics, static /readyz, no rate limit, no global exception handler, hardcoded bind.

title: Session cookie is unsigned JSON; role and userId are trusted from the client
description: ws_session is encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify({token,expiresAt,role,userId})) with no HMAC or encryption. Any caller can hand-craft a cookie with role:'admin' and a far-future expiresAt to pass the portal and admin gates and to drive the proxy and capture endpoints. The engine still verifies the bearer token (api/auth.py:31), so real engine data is protected by the engine JWT alone, but portal authorization, the capture handoff endpoints, and all sample/inline pages are reachable with a forged cookie, and there is no middleware.ts to centralise checks.
what_to_do: Store only the engine JWT in a signed/encrypted cookie (iron-session or jose HMAC with a server secret), derive role from the verified JWT claims or from GET /auth/me, and add a middleware.ts that validates on every portal/admin/api request.
verifier_evidence: lib/auth.ts:22 JSON.parse(decodeURIComponent(cookie)) with no signature check; :23 trusts client-supplied expiresAt; :31 writes plain JSON. admin/audit/page.tsx:7 and admin/products/page.tsx:7-8 gate solely on session.role from that cookie; (portal)/layout.tsx:15-16 gates on presence only; proxy route :32-35 forwards session.token as Bearer. `find woundscan-web -name 'middleware.*'` returns nothing. Engine get_identity (api/auth.py:31) does verify HS256 so real data stays protected. Major is right: incremental exposure over F1 is role escalation to admin (placeholder pages), arbitrary expiry, and arbitrary userId. what_to_do is correct.

title: Progression point ordering contract inverted between engine and web
description: ProgressionResponse field names match the zod schema, but the engine returns points ascending by captured_at (verified via TestClient: points[0] is the oldest, trend.last_capture_at == points[-1].captured_at) while the web assumes points[0] is the latest. With a real engine: the wound subtitle, ReimbursementPanel prefill, NotesPanel default measurement, and the mesh page's measurementId (hence which OBJ/PDF opens) all resolve to the OLDEST capture; NotesPanel's 'prior' becomes the next-newer capture so days_since_prior clamps to 1 and prior deltas are sign-inverted in the generated note; the depth sparkline runs backwards. With the mock (built newest-first, comment wrongly calling it the engine convention) TrajectoryChart plots time right-to-left. Invisible today only because the live site never reaches an engine.
what_to_do: Keep the engine ascending (it matches trend semantics) and document it in the route docstring and lib/api.ts. In the web, normalize once: `const points = [...progression.points].sort((a,b)=>b.captured_at.localeCompare(a.captured_at))` (or sort ascending and use points.at(-1)) in wounds/[id]/page.tsx and mesh/page.tsx before deriving latest/series/depthSeries, prefer progression.trend.last_capture_at/latest_area_cm2 for the headline values, and fix NotesPanel's prior lookup to be order-independent (find the nearest earlier captured_at). Flip mockProgression to ascending so mock and engine agree. Add a vitest that feeds an engine-shaped ascending fixture through the page helpers and asserts latest.measurement_id and the prior delta sign.

Web side: wounds/[id]/page.tsx:76 `const latest = points[0]` feeds the 'Last capture' subtitle (:83) and ReimbursementPanel prefill (:187); NotesPanel.tsx:48 and :246 default to measurements[0]; :253-256 defines prior as measurements[idx+1], which under ascending order is the NEXT NEWER capture, so days_since_prior goes negative and is clamped to 1 (:273-280) and prior_* deltas are sign-inverted in the generated note body; mesh/page.tsx:36/:53 open the oldest measurement's OBJ and PDF; :67 slice(0,12).reverse() yields a descending depth series. sample.ts:145-147 builds newest-first with a comment that mislabels this as the engine convention, and TrajectoryChart.tsx plots data in array order with no sort, so the mock renders time right-to-left. No sort or normalizer exists anywhere in the web tree (grep for sort/captured_at). Severity: major stands for today's visible impact (reversed chart on the mock-only live site), but this becomes a blocker the moment API_URL points at a real engine because signed progression notes would embed inverted prior deltas and the 3D report would be for the wrong capture.

title: Phone capture handoff is an in-process Map that never reaches the engine and cannot work on Vercel
description: Sessions live in a process-local globalThis Map with a 30-minute TTL and the file is labelled 'Development-only'. On Vercel, serverless instances (and cold starts) share no memory, so the desktop POST /api/capture/sessions, the phone GET /api/capture/sessions/{id}, and the upload can land on different instances; the phone sees 'Session not found' or the desktop never observes the upload. Even on one long-lived Node process, the base64 JPEG (up to 7 MB) is held in web memory and never forwarded to the engine (no call to /uploads/presigned or /measurements anywhere in the capture code), the 'Attach to wound case' button has no handler, and none of the create/poll/image/upload routes require a session: anyone holding the 16-hex link (it is 64-bit random, so not enumerable) can read the wound image and patientLabel, and anyone can create unbounded sessions and push 7 MB payloads into memory.
what_to_do: Back the store with Redis/S3, or better, use the engine's own flow (POST /uploads/presigned -> PUT to S3 -> POST /measurements) so the capture becomes a real measurement; require a portal session on create/poll/image, keep the phone upload scoped by a signed short-lived token, rate-limit session creation, and remove 'Capture from phone' from the sidebar until it is wired. If it must stay, gate the routes on NODE_ENV!=='production' and label the page dev-only.

PRODUCTION.md:46-57 and woundscan-web/README.md:14 confirm Vercel as the deploy target; no vercel.json. One wording correction: Next 14 on Vercel generally bundles App Router routes into shared serverless functions rather than one-per-route, but concurrent instances and cold starts still share no memory, so the conclusion (desktop/phone land on different instances, 'Session not found', lost uploads) holds. Second correction: the session id is 8 random bytes (captureStore.ts:80-86), so the image endpoint is unguessable rather than enumerable; the PHI exposure is limited to anyone holding the QR link, while the unauthenticated POST is an unbounded-memory/DoS vector. Major is right.

title: Silent substitution of fabricated clinical data when the engine is absent or errors

title: No PHI retention schedule, disposal/deletion or right-to-amend workflow; every S3 object is locked for 6 years and the portal shows a fabricated retention policy

Retention periods are inconsistent: audit_log.py:7, s3.py:34 and README.md:111 say 6 years while the portal Settings page prints literals of 7 years for audit, measurements and photos, 3 years for meshes and 'indefinite (de-identified)' analytics (settings/page.tsx:89,94-98). title: Datetimes serialize with microseconds; iOS ISO8601 decoder will reject them
description: Every server-generated datetime is serialized with microseconds; the iOS client decodes all responses with JSONDecoder.dateDecodingStrategy = .iso8601, which rejects fractional seconds, so LoginResponse, Wound and MeasurementResult decoding will throw and iOS login cannot succeed against this API.
what_to_do: Either (server) add a shared pydantic base model / field_serializer that emits second-precision RFC3339 with 'Z' for all datetime fields, or (client) install a custom date decoder that tries ISO8601DateFormatter with and without .withFractionalSeconds. Add an iOS unit test decoding a real engine response fixture.

description: Sessions are stateless JWTs: logout cannot revoke, there is no idle-refresh, and every token hard-expires 15 minutes after login (clinicians get logged out mid-capture; a stolen token stays valid until then). title: Undermining volume/surface formulas are physically wrong and the module is unwired; sidewall module absent
description: V = 1/2 sum(u^2 h) dtheta integrates a wedge from the origin, not the annulus outside the wound edge; the function does not accept the wound edge radius R(theta) at all. title: Medicare estimator is CY2025-only, hardcoded, and structurally wrong for >=100 cm2 wounds and 2026 skin-substitute policy
description: The estimator is hardcoded to CY2025 (5 CPT rows, CF 32.3465) with no year tag, data file or update path; the ReimbursementSetting table exists but is never read. Product payment is added even for facility POS where the physician does not bill it, and GPCI has no locality table. As of CY2026 the CF is $33.40 non-QP / $33.57 QP and non-351 skin substitutes are paid as incident-to supplies at a flat $127.14/cm2 (corrected from $127.28) in both office and HOPD, so the ASP+6% Q-code model is obsolete for most products (351 biologics remain ASP-based). Because the module is explicitly labelled an estimator (billing.py:3-4) and every note line says 'estimate only - verify on remittance', the core device can ship with it disabled; it is not a production blocker for the platform, but it is a major feature defect: estimates can be off by an order of magnitude for the product component and a wrong dollar figure is written into signed notes.

Then: move RVUs/CF/GPCI into a versioned data file or the reimbursement_settings table keyed by year and effective date (load CMS PFS RVU and GPCI files); select 15271/15272 vs 15273/15274 (and 15275-15278) by total wound area per CPT; implement the CY2026 incident-to supply payment ($127.14/cm2 for PMA/510(k)/361 HCT/P products, ASP path only for 351 biologics) with a year switch; zero physician product payment for facility POS; add unit tests pinned to published national rates for both years.

title: Graft area formula double-counts the perimeter offset term
description: A_graft = S + 2*delta*P + 4*delta^2 double-counts the perimeter offset: the true offset area is S + delta*P + 4*delta^2 (rectangle) or S + delta*P + pi*delta^2 (convex/rounded), so required_cm2 is inflated by delta*P (25-50% for typical wounds), which changes the selected stock size in the PDF/API and over-orders material worth ~$127/cm2 under CY2026 rates. The docs and tests repeat the formula without justification.
what_to_do: Confirm intent with the clinical/regulatory owner; correct sizing.py (and the notes string at sizing.py:91), README.md:78 and docs/math_reference.md:168 to S + delta*P + pi*delta^2 (or keep 4*delta^2 as a documented conservative corner term); if a deliberate safety margin is wanted, express it explicitly (e.g. a margin factor) and disclose it in the PDF methodology text; add a unit test pinning the coefficient against a rectangle and circle.
verifier_evidence: sizing.py:3-4 and :74,:78-80 use S + 2*delta*P + 4*delta^2 with the actual polygon perimeter (pipeline.py:214-215,:282). README.md:78 and docs/math_reference.md:168 state the same formula. Derivation: offsetting a w x h rectangle by delta on every side gives (w+2d)(h+2d) = S + 2d(w+h) + 4d^2 = S + d*P + 4d^2 with P=2(w+h); a circle gives pi(r+d)^2 = S + d*P + pi*d^2; for any convex footprint the Steiner formula is S + d*P + pi*d^2. The code's 2*d*P term therefore overstates by exactly d*P. Reproduced numerically: 5x5 cm, d=0.5 -> true 36.0 vs code 46.0 (+28%); d=2.0 -> 81.0 vs 121.0 (+49%); circle r=2.82, d=0.5 -> 34.6 vs 43.7 (+26%). Live pipeline: SA 13.4 cm2, P 12.5 cm, d=0.5 -> required 28.3 cm2 selects 50 cm2 stock, whereas the correct ~21 cm2 (+2 sigma) fits a 25 cm2 stock. tests/unit/test_graft.py and REQ-GFT-001/002 only assert monotonicity, so correcting the coefficient breaks no traceability test.

title: REQ-INV-005 tests point-estimate-in-CI, not truth coverage
description: REQ-INV-005's test cannot fail by construction (the 95% CI of a symmetric MC distribution always contains its own centre); the analytic truth is never used and no hit-rate is measured, so a traced regulatory requirement ('95% CIs contain the truth >=95%') has no supporting evidence. This is the same defect class as G1 at smaller scope (4 of 33 cases) and, being in the regulatory matrix, warrants major rather than minor.
what_to_do: Replace with a real calibration test: for N=200 trials draw depth_obs = true_depth + N(0, sigma) inside the mask, run compute_volume_with_uncertainty on depth_obs, count trials whose CI contains w.true_volume, and assert the hit-rate is within a binomial band around 0.95 (e.g. 0.90-0.99); keep a cheap single-trial truth-in-CI assertion as the fast commit gate; update validation_protocol.md:28 and regulatory_traceability.md:19 to state the trial count and acceptance band.
verifier_evidence: test_property_invariants.py:72-83 asserts ci_95_low <= compute_volume(same depth) <= ci_95_high for seeds 0-3; w.true_volume unused; regulatory_traceability.md:19 'REQ-INV-005 95% CI contains truth (low noise)'; validation_protocol.md:28 '95% CIs contain the truth >=95%'. REPRODUCED (n_grid=51, std 0.02 cm, 400 samples): point estimate 9.4261 vs analytic truth 9.4248 (discretisation error 0.014%), CI half-width 0.0139 cm3 (0.15%); over 50 seeds point-in-CI 50/50 (tautological: volume is linear in depth so the MC distribution is centred on the point estimate) and truth-in-CI also 50/50, so the auditor's proposed assertion passes today and is strictly stronger. Neither variant measures calibration: the input depth is never perturbed per trial, only the MC RNG.
root_cause: REQ-INV-005 asserts point-estimate-in-CI, never coverage rate versus truth; CI inputs are unfitted constants.

title: Burst capture can hang forever and holds ~60 full-resolution frames in memory
description: The burst continuation has no timeout or cancellation and burstActive is never reset on failure, so a stalled burst hangs the capture step permanently (second attempt throws NSError code 1). Retaining 60 full-resolution capturedImage buffers is not just a memory risk: it starves ARKit's camera buffer pool, which makes the stall likely rather than hypothetical.
what_to_do: Convert each frame as it arrives inside session(_:didUpdate:) (copy depth/confidence into Data with the G8 header, keep only the single best RGB frame encoded to JPEG immediately) instead of retaining CVPixelBuffers; add a Task-based timeout (e.g. 8 s) that resumes the continuation with an error and resets burstActive; honour Task cancellation via withTaskCancellationHandler; reset burstActive in every exit path.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-ios/WoundScan/Capture/ARKitCapture.swift:64-66 burstActive guard/set (reset only at :106 on success); :69-73 withCheckedThrowingContinuation with no timeout or Task-cancellation handling; :93 `guard self.burstActive, let depth = depthOpt else { return }` skips frames without depth; :94-101 retains CapturedFrame(depth: ARDepthData, pixelBuffer: frame.capturedImage) for up to 60 frames. Retaining capturedImage CVPixelBuffers from consecutive ARFrames holds ARKit's camera buffer pool; ARKit stops delivering frames once the pool is exhausted (the 'ARSession is retaining N ARFrames' condition), so the burst very likely stalls before 60 frames, and with no timeout the shutter Task never returns.

title: Mesh viewer Z-sign convention is inverted relative to the engine; only the bundled demo OBJ renders correctly
description: The engine emits OBJ with +Z = depth (z >= 0, deepest = largest z) and expects the viewer to flip Z; the iOS viewer does. MeshCanvas only centres, scales and applies rotateX(-pi/2), which maps engine +Z onto scene +Y (up). It then assumes 'more negative Y = deeper'. That is only true for public/demo-wound.obj, whose z values are negative (deepest = -12 at the centre). A real engine mesh therefore renders as an upward dome: the crater apex becomes the highest point, the heat/depth/tissue ramps colour the shallow rim as 'deepest' and the true deepest region as 'shallowest', and the cross-section clip removes the deep half instead of the shallow rim. BBoxAxes additionally draws the W and D lines on the wrong axes because it uses the pre-rotation bounding box. Today the only way an engine OBJ reaches the viewer is a real JWT session on a wound whose mesh the engine has cached (the demo token gets a 401 -> demo OBJ, non-UUID ids get 422 -> demo OBJ), so the defect is invisible in demo mode and in the public /demo, tour and DemoSection embeds, all of which use the bundled OBJ. The measured numbers (depth, volume, area) shown next to the mesh come from the engine and are unaffected; the defect is a misleading visualisation of the core 3D feature, not a broken page.
what_to_do: In WoundMesh's useMemo, after merging and before rotateX, apply merged.scale(1,1,-1) (or negate Z in the position attribute) so engine +Z sinks to -Y; material is already DoubleSide and computeVertexNormals runs afterwards, so winding is not an issue. Regenerate public/demo-wound.obj with the engine's grid_to_obj (positive z) so all four consumers (proxy fallback, /demo, DemoSection, tour ScanView) share the engine convention, and fix the comment at MeshCanvas.tsx:197-201. Rewrite BBoxAxes to read the post-rotation bounding box (x = length, y = depth, z = width) and label accordingly. Add a vitest that parses public/demo-wound.obj and a grid_to_obj fixture, runs the same normalisation, and asserts the crater minimum lands at the most negative Y. Consider promoting to blocker once engine-produced meshes are routinely served to clinicians.
estimate: 3-4 hours incl. verification against an engine-produced OBJ

title: Proxy 3s abort spans body streaming and swaps in the demo mesh on any engine error, with no visible indicator
description: AbortSignal.timeout(3000) is attached to the upstream fetch whose body is then streamed to the client; large OBJ/PDF responses that take longer than 3s will be truncated mid-stream. PDF links ('PDF ↗', 'Generate Report') open a tab showing 503/422 JSON when the engine is down.

Apply the timeout to headers only (race the fetch, then stream without the signal) or raise it substantially for mesh/pdf paths. In MeshWorkspace fetch the mesh with fetch(), read x-ws-demo, show a visible 'Demo mesh' badge, and hand the text to OBJLoader.parse. Give the PDF links an error state instead of opening raw JSON.

Server was down so not reproduced over HTTP; behaviour follows directly from the code.
root_cause: The catch-all proxy relays any path with no size cap and, together with the wound pages, silently substitutes demo mesh/mockProgression on any engine error.

title: UploadService is not the durable offline queue its header claims; jobs are dropped silently and in-flight slots are held during backoff
description: The doc comment says every artifact is 'Persisted across app launches', but pending is an in-memory @Published array and UploadJob holds the full Data blob (60 LiDAR depth frames) in RAM. After 4 failed attempts the job is discarded with no error surfaced; because completed() runs after the Task.sleep, a job in backoff still counts against maxInFlight=3. The PUT sends no Content-Type and no integrity header, whereas the engine's own S3 writes attach x-amz-meta-sha256 (s3.py:74) -- a mismatch that will matter once a real presigned PUT exists (F4).
what_to_do: Persist the queue to disk (store file URLs under Application Support, not Data blobs) and reload in init; call completed() before the backoff sleep (or track backoff separately from inFlight); publish a `failed: [UploadJob]` list / callback so the UI can surface terminal failures; set Content-Type and whatever hash header the presign contract (F4) signs. Raise to major once F3/F4 make this code live.
verifier_evidence: UploadService.swift:3-7 doc claims persistence; :10 `@Published var pending: [UploadJob]` is in-memory; :67-73 UploadJob holds `let data: Data`. :30-44: on error the task sleeps 2^attempt seconds and requeues, then calls completed() (line 43) only after the sleep, so inFlight (max 3, line 15) is held during backoff; when attempt reaches 4 the job is dropped with no error surfaced. :48-51 PUT sets no Content-Type or hash header, while s3.py:64-70 writes ContentType plus Metadata sha256 for the engine's own puts.

title: iOS: token never persisted (Keychain stub), raw JWT seeded into a non-secure WKWebView cookie, unused Photos permission, no offline queue
description: AuthService.loadPersisted returns nil and save/signOut are empty, so the bearer token exists only in AppState memory — not in Keychain and not in UserDefaults (grep finds neither). That is accidentally safe but means every launch requires re-login. PortalWebView writes the raw JWT into a 'ws_session' cookie with secure=false and a 12-hour expiry inside the persistent default WKWebsiteDataStore; the web tier expects JSON so JSON.parse fails and the SSO path is dead, but the token still sits on disk in the WebKit cookie store. Info.plist has no ATS exceptions (HTTPS enforced) but requests NSPhotoLibraryUsage although no Photos API is used. Depth/confidence blobs (60 frames) are held in memory only; the 'persist locally'/'persisted across launches' docstrings are not implemented, so there is no encrypted offline queue.
what_to_do: Implement Keychain storage (kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly) and clear it on signOut; stop seeding the cookie or seed the exact server-issued cookie over HTTPS with secure=true and the JWT's real expiry; drop NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription; if an offline queue is added, use FileProtectionType.complete and purge after upload.
verifier_evidence: AuthService.swift:19-30 loadPersisted() returns nil and save()/signOut() are empty stubs; grep finds no Keychain/UserDefaults usage anywhere in WoundScan -- token lives only in AppState memory. PortalWebView.swift:22 takes sessionCookie and 55-64 seeds an 'ws_session' HTTPCookie with .secure=false and a 12h expiry into the default (persistent) WKWebsiteDataStore (config.websiteDataStore=.default()); the web tier JSON.parses the cookie so this raw-JWT value fails parse (dead SSO path) yet persists on disk in the WebKit cookie store. Info.plist:29-30 declares NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription though no Photos API is used. UploadService.swift docstring claims 'Persisted across app launches' but pending is an in-memory @Published array with no persistence. Accurate; minor.

title: Direct server-side engine fetches have no timeout

verifier_evidence: wounds/[id]/page.tsx:29-32 and mesh/page.tsx:18-21 call fetch with cache:'no-store' and no signal; proxy/route.ts:54 uses AbortSignal.timeout(3000) and login/route.ts:20 AbortSignal.timeout(1500). On Vercel a black-holed API_URL would block the server render until the function's max duration rather than a fetch timeout. Minor is right; folds into F8's shared client.

title: Global Permissions-Policy camera=() disables getUserMedia on the mobile capture page
description: next.config.mjs applies Permissions-Policy: camera=() to every path including /m/:id, which denies getUserMedia to the page's own origin. MobileCapture feature-detects the API (:41-45), so it enters the 'ready-cam' phase, getUserMedia rejects, and the catch (:74-76) drops to the file-picker phase. The `<input type=file capture="environment">` fallback (:191-201) is HTML Media Capture and is not governed by Permissions-Policy, so the phone still opens its native camera and uploads succeed. Only the live viewfinder path is dead in production, with a visible flash of the camera pane on first load and on each Retake.
what_to_do: Change the header to camera=(self) (keep microphone=() and geolocation=()), or add a second headers() entry that omits Permissions-Policy for /m/:path*. Optionally short-circuit the flash by checking `document.featurePolicy?.allowsFeature('camera')` before entering 'ready-cam'.
verifier_evidence: next.config.mjs:8 source '/(.*)' matches /m/:id and :14 sets Permissions-Policy camera=() (empty allowlist = denied for the page's own origin too), so navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia at MobileCapture.tsx:65 rejects with NotAllowedError. However :41-45 only feature-detects, and the catch at :74-76 sets phase 'ready-file', whose input at :191-201 is `<input type="file" accept="image/*" capture="environment">`. HTML Media Capture (the capture attribute) is not a Permissions-Policy-controlled feature, so the phone still launches its native camera app and the upload path (:116-132) completes. Net effect in production: the in-page viewfinder/'Take photo' branch is unreachable and the user sees a brief flash of the ready-cam pane before the file picker appears (also on every 'Retake'/'Try again', which set phase back to 'ready-cam'). That is a UX degradation, not a broken capture flow, so major overstates it.

title: API client is dead, split across two env vars, and POST responses are not validated
description: apiFetch reads NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL and has no callers; five files each declare their own API_BASE from API_URL with inconsistent timeouts (1.5 s, 3 s, none x3). API_BASE from API_URL is declared in login/route.ts:4, proxy/route.ts:6, phantom/submit/route.ts:4, wounds/[id]/page.tsx:20, mesh/page.tsx:11 (five files) with timeouts 1.5 s, 3 s, none, none, none. GraftPanel.tsx:136, NotesPanel.tsx:316, ReimbursementPanel.tsx:51 consume res.json() unparsed. One addition: PRODUCTION.md:54 and RUNBOOK.md:340 instruct operators to set NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL in Vercel, so the browser-exposed variable is a documented step, not a hypothetical; it is not a secret and the engine already allows CORS *, so this remains minor.

title: Monte Carlo correlated-noise sampler is loosely tied to the GP posterior
description: The correlated path smooths white noise with mode='constant' then divides by a single global std, so border pixels are under-dispersed and the Gaussian-kernel sigma is treated as equal to the Matern lengthscale the pipeline passes in; non-negativity clipping biases the mean upward near the wound edge. CI widths are therefore only heuristically related to the GP posterior.
what_to_do: Either draw samples from the actual GP posterior (Cholesky of K_post on the masked grid, or via random Fourier features) or, if keeping the smoothing approach, compute the exact per-pixel variance of the smoothed field (or use mode='reflect'/'nearest') for rescaling and map the Matern 5/2 lengthscale to an equivalent Gaussian sigma; document the non-negativity clipping bias near the wound edge.
verifier_evidence: uncertainty.py:151-168 (gaussian_filter with mode='constant', sigma_pix = correlation_length/dx i.e. Matern lengthscale used directly as Gaussian sigma, then divided by one global np.std), :172-173 (np.maximum(samples, 0) when enforce_nonneg). pipeline.py:225 and :234 pass gp.correlation_length_mm/10 as correlation_length_cm. Reproduced on a 60x60 field with unit std and correlation_length 0.5 cm (5 px): per-pixel sample std 0.99 at centre, 0.80 at an edge pixel, 0.57 at a corner; with mean 0.2 and std 1 the clipped sample mean is 0.496 (bias +0.30).

title: All quality/validation thresholds are assumed constants with no data derivation and internal doc/code mismatches

what_to_do: Centralise thresholds in one config module with provenance comments (source study or phantom run id), align the docstrings, run the synthetic/phantom suites to justify at least the grade cutoffs and plausibility bound, and record a thresholds version in provenance.
verifier_evidence: quality/confidence.py:14-17 'version-locked... regulatory deviation' and :34-41 weights; validation/quality_score.py:50-57 cutoffs 0.85/0.70/0.50, :84-97 anchor/fiducial mappings, :113-121 weights; temporal_plausibility.py:3-5 docstring '~10% heal / ~30% worsen per day' vs :32-33 symmetric abs 0.15 volume / 0.10 area; plausibility.py:9 'x1.2' vs :53 '*1.05'; phantom_calibration.py:68 drift_alert_threshold_pct=3.0 vs docs/validation_protocol.md:49 '<2% volume error'; specularity.py:27-28 0.85/0.20; lighting.py:31 sigma=15, :38 exp(-20x); edge_proximity.py:18 5 mm; frame_consistency.py:16 1 mm. No threshold cites a source or study.

title: U-Net inference path is not production-safe
description: U-Net path: torch.load without weights_only=True (arbitrary pickle on torch 2.2-2.5), no crop/resize/pad to a multiple of 8 so arbitrary image sizes fail at the skip-connection cat, no input normalisation, full-resolution CPU inference. Heuristic: hue distance ignores wrap-around, so pure red (hue 0) scores 1.0 but any red with a slight blue component (hue just under 1.0, e.g. RGB(255,0,8)) scores ~0.
what_to_do: Add preprocessing (crop/resize to 1024, ImageNet-style normalisation matching training), pass weights_only=True, pad to a multiple of 8 and crop back, and change red_score to use circular hue distance min(h, 1-h).
verifier_evidence: boundary_segmentation.py:150-152 torch.load(str(path), map_location=...) without weights_only (pyproject.toml:47 torch>=2.2; default flipped to weights_only=True only in 2.6); :84-92 three MaxPool2d stages with skip cats so H,W must be multiples of 8 (e.g. H=65 -> up1 output 64 vs e1 65 -> cat fails), no pad/resize anywhere; :170 only /255 scaling, no mean/std normalisation; docs/ml_models.md:8 says 1024x1024 crop but nothing crops; :189 red_score=(1-|h-0|)*s. Reproduced hue wrap: RGB(255,0,0) hue=0.0 -> red_score 1.0; RGB(255,0,8) hue=0.9948 -> 0.0052; RGB(255,0,20) -> 0.013; a uniform (255,0,8) image gives confidence max 0.005 and an empty mask at the 0.4 threshold. Torch path could not be executed (torch not installed).

title: Plausibility box-bound check passes any volume when max_depth is 0
description: The 'or upper_bound == 0' escape makes the box-bound check pass any volume when footprint or max_depth is 0 (verified V=99 cm3 passes). Unreachable through the current pipeline (V and max_depth come from the same grid) but wrong for any other caller and masks exactly the inconsistency the check exists for.
what_to_do: Replace the escape with: passed = volume_cm3 <= upper_bound if upper_bound > 0 else volume_cm3 <= 1e-9; add a unit test for V>0 with max_depth=0.
verifier_evidence: validation/plausibility.py:53-59 'passed=volume_cm3 <= upper_bound or upper_bound == 0'. Reproduced: run_geometric_plausibility_checks(99.0, 10.0, 10.0, 0.0, 0.0) -> volume_le_box_upper_bound passed=True (all six checks pass). In the pipeline path this cannot trigger a false pass because max_depth_cm is the max over the same clipped depth grid that V integrates (pipeline.py:195,212,217), so V>0 implies max_depth>0; the escape only matters for direct callers.

title: Motion-artifact thresholds have a units bug (mm vs mm/s) that saturates any real burst
description: Thresholds labelled mm/deg are compared against per-second rates, so any realistic handheld 30 fps burst saturates the motion term at 1.0 (verified: 1 mm + 0.5 deg per frame -> 1.0; 0.1 mm/frame -> 0.6). Latent: the module is only reachable via compute_quality_components, which nothing in the pipeline calls; it becomes a major confidence-map bug the moment G4 is wired.
what_to_do: Fix before wiring G4: either compare per-frame deltas without dividing by dt (blur is per-exposure) or rename the parameters to *_per_s and derive values from exposure time x angular/linear velocity on real capture data; add tests at 30 fps with 0.1-1 mm and 0.05-0.5 deg per frame. Escalate to major when the confidence map is connected to the pipeline.
verifier_evidence: quality/motion.py:34-35 thresholds translation_threshold_mm=5.0 / rotation_threshold_deg=2.0; :51-53 deltas divided by dt (so mm/s and deg/s); :57-59 score=min(1, max_rate/threshold). Reproduced with 5-pose bursts at 30 fps: 1.0 mm + 0.5 deg per frame -> 1.000; 0.1 mm/frame -> 0.600; 0.1 deg/frame alone -> 1.000. tests/unit/test_quality.py:62-67 only tests 50 mm in 0.1 s. Reachability: compute_motion_artifact is called only from quality/confidence.py:93 (compute_quality_components), which has no callers in src (G4), so the bug cannot affect any production output today.

title: reportlab markup injection via unescaped product names, rationale and provenance text
description: Product names are interpolated into reportlab mini-XML unescaped. Bare '<' and '&' are tolerated by reportlab 5, but unbalanced or recognised tags in a name (, unclosed /, ) make /pdf 500, recognised tags restyle the report, and makes reportlab open a server-side file path. Rationale is not rendered so it is not an injection surface. Exposure grows once names become admin-entered (G3).
what_to_do: Escape every interpolated string (product name, ids, provenance values) with xml.sax.saxutils.escape before building Paragraphs, and add a unit test with '' and '
verifier_evidence: pdf_report.py:141-144 interpolates product_name unescaped inside ...; :163 methodology is a literal; :168 provenance lines go through Paragraph. Rationale is never rendered. Reproduced with reportlab 5.0.1: 'Size <5 cm', 'a < b > c', 'A & B', '&foo; y', 'tag', 'big' all render (the last two are interpreted as markup, i.e. styling injection); 'AlgiDuo Large', 'AlgiDuo', 'AlgiDuo x' raise ValueError; "" raises OSError because reportlab tries to open the path (a product name could make the server embed a local image file into the PDF). Provenance only raises if it contains such tags, which is not user-controlled today.

title: CI never executes the torch or testcontainers tests (the 5 skips)
description: The three torch U-Net tests are certainly never executed in CI (no [ml] install anywhere). The claim that 'no job provides a Docker daemon' is inaccurate for GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest, which has one by default; the two testcontainers Postgres tests most likely do run in the unit-and-regulatory job (unverified: CI logs expired). The local '5 skipped' reflects this sandbox, not CI. Residual gap: the skip is silent, so a runner without Docker would hide the only real-Postgres schema checks without failing.
what_to_do: Add a CPU-torch job installing '.[dev,ml]' for the U-Net tests. For Postgres, make the daemon requirement explicit in CI (e.g. if CI=1 then fail instead of skip when Docker is unreachable, or use `services: postgres` with a WS_TEST_PG_URL fixture) so the tests cannot silently skip; optionally publish skip counts in the job summary.

But the docker SDK (7.2.0) and testcontainers ARE installed by [dev], and GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest (engine-ci.yml:38) ships a running Docker daemon, so _testcontainers_available() would return True there and the two Postgres tests would execute in CI. title: Health checks are static; readiness does not verify DB/S3

title: Warmup readiness is fake; double ARSession start; no LiDAR runtime gate or user message
description: Readiness is a fixed timer, pipeline.start() runs twice, and on non-LiDAR iPhones ARKitCapture.start() returns silently while CapturePipeline still reports .ready, so 'Start capture' enables and the user reaches BurstCaptureView with a shutter that can never enable (distanceMm stays nil) and no explanation. The App Store cannot restrict to LiDAR devices via plist; the description text is the only gate.
what_to_do: Gate .ready on arkit.isReady && trackingState == .normal (observe via Combine); remove the onAppear start (keep .task); in CapturePipeline.start check ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth) and set stage = .failed with a user-facing alert ('This app requires an iPhone with a LiDAR scanner') when false; wire ARKitCapture.frameCount into .capturing(progress:). Do not rely on 'iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12' for LiDAR gating; adding it is optional and only trims A11-and-older devices.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-ios/WoundScan/Capture/CapturePipeline.swift:31-37 sets .ready after a fixed 500 ms sleep without checking arkit.isReady/trackingState; CaptureFlowView.swift:42-44 `.task { await pipeline.start() }` and WarmupView :84-86 `.onAppear { Task { await pipeline.start() } }` both call start (ARSession.run with .resetTracking twice); ARKitCapture.swift:39-42 returns silently when sceneDepth unsupported; Info.plist:37-41 UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities = [arm64, arkit]; woundscan-ios/README.md:42 claims a non-existent 'arkit.lidar' capability. Correction: 'iphone-ipad-minimum-performance-a12' is a real UIRequiredDeviceCapabilities key but only excludes pre-A12 devices; iPhone XR/XS/11/12/13/14/15/16 non-Pro are A12+ without LiDAR, so it does not gate on LiDAR. Apple has no LiDAR capability key; bin/asc-metadata.json already states the LiDAR requirement in the description.

The engine already has GET /wounds (list) that the wounds page could use.

title: OTLP tracing depends on implicit OTEL_* env but the exporter package is not installed, so tracing is silently disabled everywhere
description: The `except Exception: pass` around the exporter import hides the missing opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http dependency, and FastAPIInstrumentor is never applied to the app, so tracing is silently disabled everywhere regardless of OTEL_* env. Error reporting is intentionally structlog-only (no Sentry DSN), which is fine for HIPAA but means no env var exists for alerting.
what_to_do: Add opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http to dependencies, call FastAPIInstrumentor.instrument_app(app) in create_app(), read OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT explicitly, and log a warning rather than swallowing the ImportError.
verifier_evidence: monitoring/tracing.py:43-50 wraps the OTLPSpanExporter import in `except Exception: pass` (not a bare `except:`); pyproject.toml:39-41 lists opentelemetry-api/sdk/instrumentation-fastapi but no opentelemetry-exporter-otlp*; error_reporting.py:1-8 documents the intentional no-Sentry policy. Additional: grep finds no FastAPIInstrumentor/instrument_app call anywhere in src, so opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi is installed but never applied; even with the exporter present, no request spans would be produced.

title: No secrets or .env files are tracked in git; .env handling is consistent
description: git ls-files shows no .env, .vercel, tfvars, tfstate, .p8 or key files; no .env exists on disk. pydantic-settings will read a CWD .env for WS_DB_*/WS_S3_* only, not for the os.environ-based variables (JWT, dev login, Celery), which is an inconsistency worth knowing when writing local .env files.
what_to_do: Consolidate all WS_* reads into one pydantic Settings class so .env and validation behave uniformly.
verifier_evidence: .gitignore:27-28 `.env.local` / `.env*.local`, :50 `*.tfvars`, :65-66 `.env` and `bin/.asc-env`; woundscan-web/.gitignore:1 `.vercel`. `git ls-files | grep -iE '\.env|tfvars|tfstate|\.p8$|\.pem$|\.key$|\.vercel|asc-env'` returns nothing and `find` shows no .env* on disk. storage/postgres.py:45 and storage/s3.py:25 set env_file='.env' with prefixes WS_DB_/WS_S3_, while WS_JWT_SIGNING_KEY, WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN, WS_DEV_*, WS_CELERY_* are read via os.environ (api/auth.py:18, routes/auth.py:80-88, worker.py:20-23), confirming the inconsistency.

title: ProbeRecord serialises an extra 'id' key; tolerated only because engine models use pydantic's default extra='ignore'
description: ProbeRecord is Identifiable with var id: UUID = UUID() and Codable with synthesized keys, so each probe_measurements entry carries an 'id' field absent from ProbeMeasurementInput. No engine model sets model_config extra='forbid', so it is dropped, but tightening validation server-side would start rejecting iOS payloads.
what_to_do: Give ProbeRecord explicit CodingKeys that omit `id` (keep it as a local Identifiable UUID), or add an engine contract test that validates an iOS-shaped payload so switching to extra='forbid' later cannot silently break the app.
verifier_evidence: CaptureSession.swift:31-32 `struct ProbeRecord: Codable, Equatable, Identifiable { var id: UUID = UUID() ... }` with synthesized keys, so JSONEncoder.iso (convertToSnakeCase) emits an 'id' member. measurement.py:11-20 ProbeMeasurementInput has no 'id' and no model_config; verified with the installed pydantic that model_validate({...,'id':...}) succeeds and drops the key (model_config.get('extra') is None -> default 'ignore'), and a full iOS-shaped CreateMeasurementRequest with an 'id' inside probe_measurements returns 201.

title: No cross-repo contract tests: iOS tests never decode engine JSON, engine tests only run with the dev-login flag
description: iOS tests only encode ProbeRecord/BoundaryRecord/CameraIntrinsicsRecord and never round-trip a LoginResponse or MeasurementResponse fixture, which is exactly where F1 lives. Engine integration tests exercise /auth/login, /uploads/presigned and /measurements only under WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=1. CreateMeasurementPayload's comment asserts it matches CreateMeasurementRequest 1:1 with nothing enforcing that.
what_to_do: Emit app.openapi() as a checked-in snapshot in engine CI; add an XCTest target that decodes recorded LoginResponse/MeasurementResponse JSON (with fractional-second timestamps) and encodes CreateMeasurementPayload for validation against that schema; change ios-ci.yml to run `xcodebuild test` and drop the `|| echo` so failures are visible.
verifier_evidence: WoundScanTests/CaptureSessionTests.swift:5-28 only encodes ProbeRecord/BoundaryRecord and round-trips CameraIntrinsicsRecord; no LoginResponse/MeasurementResult fixture is decoded. .github/workflows/ios-ci.yml:30-38 runs `xcodebuild ... build` (not `test`) and swallows failure with `|| echo`. tests/integration/test_api.py:14 sets WS_ALLOW_DEV_LOGIN=1 and never exercises POST /measurements. CreateMeasurementPayload.swift:3-4 asserts a 1:1 match with nothing enforcing it.

title: Controls verified as correctly implemented
description: bcrypt via passlib; 256-bit urlsafe session ids; jwt.decode pins algorithms=['HS256'] (no alg-confusion); TOTP with +/-1 window and digit/length check; notes and grafts routes correctly scope by organization_id; pydantic regex/ge constraints on enumerated inputs; S3 public-access block and versioning; RDS security group ingress only from the ECS task SG; ECS and RDS in private subnets behind NAT with public subnets not auto-assigning IPs; ALB drops invalid header fields and uses the TLS1.3 policy; VPC flow logs and GuardDuty/SecurityHub in prod; portal cookie is httpOnly + sameSite=strict; portal pages are noindex; no third-party error reporter receives exception payloads.
what_to_do: Keep; these are the patterns the blockers above should be aligned to.
verifier_evidence: Spot-checked the cited positives: identity.py:41-54 bcrypt via passlib; sessions.py:67 secrets.token_urlsafe(32) session ids; sessions.py:98 jwt.decode pins algorithms=['HS256'] (no alg-confusion); mfa.py:15-22 TOTP with valid_window=1 and digit/length check; s3/main.tf:52-58 public-access block + versioning (23-28); rds SG ingress only from app SG (54-62); vpc private subnets behind NAT with public map_public_ip_on_launch=false (44-59); alb drop_invalid_header_fields=true (77) and TLS1.3 policy (134); auth.ts:32-34 cookie httpOnly+sameSite=strict; (portal)/layout.tsx noindex; error_reporting.py:3-7 no third-party reporter. All verified correct. One imprecision: the evidence cites grafts.py:404 but that file is only 201 lines (grafts org-scoping is actually at lines 150/163/184); notes.py:224 is correct. Substance is accurate; info.

title: Logout does not revoke the engine session; engine JWT check ignores its session store
description: Web logout only deletes the cookie and never calls POST /auth/logout; the engine's logout itself only audits and does not delete the session, and verify_jwt checks only signature and exp (SessionStore is defined and exported but never used), so a bearer remains valid for its full 15-minute lifetime after logout (verified: /auth/me returns 200 after /auth/logout). Engine CORS is allow_origins=['*'] with credentials disabled; harmless while all calls are server-side.
what_to_do: Instantiate a SessionStore (Redis in prod) in the engine, have login put(), logout delete(), and get_identity get()+touch() by claims['sid']; then call /auth/logout from the web logout page before clearing the cookie. Restrict CORS to the portal origin before any browser-direct use.
verifier_evidence: logout/page.tsx:5 only clearSession(). Engine routes/auth.py:94-106 logout writes an audit entry and never touches a session store; sessions.py:92-100 verify_jwt only decodes HS256; grep shows SessionStore is exported from auth/__init__.py but never instantiated or consulted anywhere in src/woundscan. Reproduced with TestClient: POST /auth/logout -> 200, then GET /auth/me with the same bearer -> 200. main.py:42-48 CORS allow_origins=['*'], allow_credentials=False. Info is acceptable given the 15-minute lifetime (sessions.py:11), but what_to_do should note that the engine's own logout is also a no-op, so calling it from the web alone would not revoke anything.

title: No web tests and no contract tests between zod schemas and pydantic models
description: The web test script is vitest --passWithNoTests and no *.test.* files exist, so CI only lints, typechecks and builds. Engine integration tests exercise the routes but nothing asserts the shapes the web's zod schemas expect, which is how the ordering mismatch in F3 went unnoticed.
what_to_do: Export the engine's OpenAPI JSON in CI and add a vitest suite that parses recorded engine responses (or generated examples) through every zod schema in lib/api.ts, including an ordering assertion for progression points.
verifier_evidence: woundscan-web/package.json:11 test = 'vitest run --passWithNoTests'; find for *.test.* / *.spec.* under woundscan-web (excluding node_modules) returns nothing; .github/workflows/web-ci.yml:24-28 runs install, lint, typecheck, test --if-present, build. Engine has tests/integration/test_api.py and test_api_extended.py. The F3 ordering mismatch is exactly the kind of contract drift such a suite would catch (and my TestClient repro is a ready-made fixture). Info is right.
root_cause: No cross-component contract tests: iOS never decodes engine JSON, web has zero tests, zod/pydantic schemas are never diffed.

title: Dependency licensing is clean (no GPL/AGPL); engine declares Proprietary; LGPL only via psycopg2-binary and sharp's bundled libvips; no third-party notices generated
description: Python venv (147 dists): only psycopg2-binary is LGPL ('LGPL with exceptions', dynamically linked, permitted for proprietary use) and setuptools lacks license metadata. Node (568 installed packages): 469 MIT, 45 ISC, 25 Apache-2.0, 14 BSD, 4 BlueOak, plus MPL-2.0/CC0/CC-BY-4.0/Python-2.0 singles; the LGPL entries are @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64 and -linuxmusl-x64 1.3.2 (LGPL-3.0-or-later) and @img/sharp-wasm32 0.35.3 (Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT); package-lock.json also pins the other eight @img/sharp-libvips-* platform builds and three @img/sharp-win32-* packages under LGPL terms for other platforms. All come from sharp, which the app never imports (web-portal-G11). webgl-constants@1.1.1 has no license field (busboy@1.6.0 and streamsearch@1.1.0 lack one in the lockfile but ship MIT license files). No GPL/AGPL anywhere. Fonts used by the OG script ship with their OFL texts. There is no LICENSE file at the repo root and no generated third-party notice.
what_to_do: Remove sharp (already recommended) to drop the LGPL binaries; add a CI step (pip-licenses / license-checker) that fails on GPL/AGPL/unknown and emits a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES file; add a root LICENSE/proprietary notice.
verifier_evidence: pyproject.toml:11 license = {text = 'Proprietary'}, :12-43 dependency list incl. psycopg2-binary — confirmed. scripts/fonts contains JetBrainsMono-OFL.txt, Outfit-OFL.txt, WorkSans-OFL.txt (line 1 is the JetBrains copyright) — confirmed. No LICENSE file at repo root (ls -a) — confirmed. Re-ran the checks: woundscan-engine/.venv has 147 dist-info entries (not 148); the only GPL-family license is psycopg2-binary ('LGPL with exceptions'); setuptools is the only dist without license metadata — matches. woundscan-web/node_modules has 568 installed package roots (not 551): 469 MIT, 45 ISC, 25 Apache-2.0, 7 BSD-3, 7 BSD-2, 4 BlueOak, 1 each Python-2.0/MPL-2.0/CC-BY-4.0/CC0-1.0; GPL-family installed = @img/sharp-libvips-linux-x64 1.3.2 and @img/sharp-libvips-linuxmusl-x64 1.3.2 (LGPL-3.0-or-later) PLUS @img/sharp-wasm32 0.35.3 ('Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later AND MIT'), which the finding omitted; the only installed package with no license field is webgl-constants@1.1.1 — matches. package-lock.json (662 entries) additionally declares LGPL-3.0-or-later for all ten @img/sharp-libvips-* platform packages and 'Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-or-later' for the three @img/sharp-win32-* packages (optional platform deps), and lacks a license field for busboy@1.6.0 and streamsearch@1.1.0 as well as webgl-constants. No GPL/AGPL anywhere — the headline negative claim reproduces. sharp is not imported in src or scripts (grep), consistent with web-portal-G11.

title: Git history contains no secrets, keys, tokens or .env files (verified across all 118 commits)
description: Searched every added line in `git log --all -p` (126 commits across all refs; 118 on HEAD/origin/main) for AWS access-key ids, private-key blocks, JWT-shaped strings, GitHub/Slack/Stripe/Google token prefixes, aws_secret_access_key assignments and ASC key ids, and every path ever added for .env/.pem/.p8/.p12/.key/.tfvars/credential/mobileprovision names. The only hits are an example key id in a comment (bin/ship-ios:11), a test-fixture password (test_postgres_storage.py:66), placeholder tokens ('opaque', 'demo-session-token') and an attribute pass-through (s3.py:55); no real value has ever been committed. This extends contract-env-secrets-F15 (which checked HEAD only) to the full history including unmerged chore/* branches.
what_to_do: Add gitleaks (or GitHub secret scanning push protection) as a required check so this stays true; nothing to remediate.
verifier_evidence: Cited lines: bin/ship-ios:11 '#   export ASC_API_KEY_ID=ABCDE12345' (example), tests/unit/test_postgres_storage.py:66 password='hunter2' (fixture), s3.py:55 aws_secret_access_key=self.settings.secret_access_key (attribute pass-through), .gitignore:65-66 '.env' and 'bin/.asc-env' — all confirmed. Reproduced the history scan over all refs: git rev-list --all --count = 126 (HEAD/origin/main = 118; main = 109; the extra commits are on unmerged origin/chore/* branches), so '118 commits' is the HEAD count, not 'all'. git log --all -p grep for AKIA/ASIA key ids, PRIVATE KEY blocks, JWT-shaped eyJ..., ghp_/github_pat_/xox*/sk_live/AIza prefixes and aws_secret_access_key value assignments: zero hits; the only AKIA/ASC_API_KEY mentions are prose in RUNBOOK/PRODUCTION docs and env-var lookups in bin/asc and bin/ship-ios. git log --all --name-only grep for .env/.pem/.p8/.p12/.key/.tfvars/credential/secret/.asc-env/mobileprovision paths: none ever committed. A masked scan for literal password/token/secret assignments finds only placeholder values (patient_token='opaque' in measurements.py:160,186, 'p-deidentified' in a test, token 'demo-session-token' in login/route.ts:49, 'hunter2'). title: OBJ mesh is an open height-field, not the 'closed surface' the docstring promises; pure-Python loops
description: The OBJ is an open height-field, not the 'closed surface' the docstring promises; the only current consumer (iOS WoundMeshView, double-sided material) renders it fine, so this is a documentation inaccuracy unless volume rendering or watertight export is planned.
what_to_do: Fix the mesh_export.py docstring; add boundary walls and a skin-plane cap only if a watertight consumer is added; vectorise with numpy only if grid sizes grow.
verifier_evidence: mesh_export.py:5 docstring says 'forming a closed surface'; :61-91 emit only the height-field triangles (one-ring extension, no walls or cap) in nested Python loops. Sole consumer woundscan-ios/WoundScan/UI/Components/WoundMeshView.swift parses v/f lines and sets mat.isDoubleSided = true (line 208), so the open sheet renders correctly; tests/unit/test_mesh_export.py::test_partial_mask_seals_at_boundary only checks the ring extension. Grids are ~16-100 cells per side so the loops are not a practical cost.
